Dynamic lens behavior was assessed using a Purkinje meter during 9-degree saccadic eye movements. Additional outcomes included visual acuity, refraction, and complications.

Results

72 eyes of 72 patients were included, comprising 31 eyes with retropupillary iris claw IOLs and 41 eyes with scleral-fixated IOLs. Mean decentration was similar between groups, with no statistically significant difference (598 ± 303 μm vs 535 ± 261 μm; P = .57). Mean tilt was lower in the iris claw group than in the scleral-fixated group, with a statistically significant difference between groups (6.52 ± 3.20 degrees vs 8.93 ± 5.02 degrees; P = .03). Across all gaze directions, iris claw lenses demonstrated greater dynamic instability, with larger postsaccadic oscillation amplitudes, longer stationary times, and lower damping ratios (all P < .001). Visual acuity, refraction, and complication rates were comparable between groups. The IOL-iris distance was smaller in the iris claw group.

Conclusions

Decentration was comparable, whereas iris claw lenses showed less tilt but greater dynamic instability than scleral-fixated lenses.

records.title: Ray-Tracing Aberrometry and the Dysfunctional Lens Index for Objective Assessment of Posterior Capsular Opacification.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Ray-Tracing Aberrometry and the Dysfunctional Lens Index for Objective Assessment of Posterior Capsular Opacification.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the dysfunctional lens index (DLI), higher-order aberrations (HOA), and modulation transfer function (MTF) from ray-tracing aberrometry as objective markers of posterior capsular opacification (PCO) and treatment response.

Setting

Two tertiary ophthalmology centers, Istanbul, Turkey.

Design

Prospective interventional study with a clear-capsule pseudophakic control group.

Methods

Eyes with visually significant PCO after uncomplicated phacoemulsification with monofocal IOL implantation underwent ray-tracing aberrometry and 4 weeks after Nd:YAG capsulotomy; one eye per patient was analysed. CDVA, DLI, total and internal HOA root mean square (RMS), Zernike components, and MTF at 5-30 cycles/degree (cpd) were compared with clear-capsule control eyes with the same IOL.

Results

Thirty-one eyes of 31 patients (mean age 66.7 years; 21 female) and 28 control eyes were included. All parameters improved after capsulotomy (all P<.001): CDVA from 0.52 to 0.10 logMAR, DLI from 3.10 to 7.20, internal HOA RMS by 66.9%. Internal coma and trefoil decreased, whereas spherical aberration was unchanged (negative control). MTF improved at all six spatial frequencies. Pre-operatively, PCO eyes were degraded relative to controls (DLI 3.35 vs 7.67; P<.001); post-operatively they matched controls (7.23 vs 7.67; P=.44). DLI correlated with internal HOA (r=-0.947) and MTF (r=+0.842) but not CDVA (r=-0.051).

Conclusions

Ray-tracing aberrometry offers an objective view of PCO-induced optical degradation. Because the DLI tracks internal aberrations and MTF yet remains independent of high-contrast acuity, it captures impairment that CDVA alone overlooks, and returns to clear-capsule levels after capsulotomy. The DLI thus serves as a useful adjunctive marker for gauging PCO-related degradation and monitoring treatment response.

records.title: Environmental Impact of Cataract Surgery Packs: Benchmarking Real-World Practice Through the ESCRS SIDICS Platform.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Environmental Impact of Cataract Surgery Packs: Benchmarking Real-World Practice Through the ESCRS SIDICS Platform.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To assess the carbon footprint of cataract surgery pack-lists entered into the Sustainability Index for Disposables in Cataract Surgery (SIDICS) online platform of the European Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgeons (ESCRS), compare real-world configurations with the ESCRS Benchmark Pack, and identify components contributing most to disposable-related emissions.

Setting

International, web-based ESCRS SIDICS platform.

Design

Retrospective observational study.

Methods

User-entered cataract surgical pack configurations recorded in SIDICS between November 2023 and April 2025 were screened according to inclusion criteria. Carbon emissions were estimated using conservative, material-specific life-cycle assessment data from Ecoinvent v3.7.1 via Ansys Granta EduPack. Pack-level emissions were compared with the ESCRS Benchmark Pack (3.91 kg CO2 equivalent), and product-category contributions were assessed. Submission to SIDICS was voluntary; therefore, the analyzed packs represent a convenience cohort.

Results

A total of 609 cataract packs were included. The median carbon footprint was 5.59 kg CO2 equivalent (interquartile range 4.88-6.70 kg). The carbon footprint of 93.3% of submitted packs exceeded that of the ESCRS Benchmark Pack (3.91 kg CO2 equivalent), whereas 6.7% met or fell below it. The median excess over the ESCRS Benchmark Pack was 1.68 kg CO2e (p < 0.001). Drapes and covers accounted for 60.3% of emissions and surgical gowns for 23.7%.

Conclusion

The carbon footprint of most cataract surgery packs submitted to SIDICS exceeded that of the ESCRS Benchmark Pack, with drapes and gowns accounting for most pack-related emissions. Standardization and selective optimization of these high-impact components may reduce emissions, while still considering patient safety. SIDICS provides a practical tool for benchmarking pack-related emissions and quantifying measurable sustainability improvements.

records.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the effect of dry eye disease (DED) and ocular surface treatment on the agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace in patients with age-related cataract.

Setting

Eye, Ear, Nose, and Throat Hospital of Fudan University, Shanghai, China.

Design

Prospective, single-center study.

Methods

A total of 313 eyes of patients with age-related cataract were included. Eyes with DED received 0.3% sodium hyaluronate eye drops for 2 weeks and were re-examined after treatment. Corneal astigmatism measurements were obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace before pupil dilation. The main parameters included keratometric corneal astigmatism, total corneal astigmatism, and their vector components. Interdevice agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, and test-retest repeatability was evaluated using within-subject standard deviation, test-retest repeatability, and intraclass correlation coefficients.

Results

Compared with the control group, eyes at DED baseline showed wider limits of agreement and poorer TRT for both scalar astigmatism parameters and vector components. After ocular surface treatment, LoA width decreased by 50.5%-62.5% for KCA and 19.9%-29.0% for TCA across the three device comparisons. KCA repeatability improved significantly after treatment for IOLMaster 700 and iTrace, whereas significant improvement in TCA repeatability was observed only for IOLMaster 700. Device- and parameter-specific differences persisted after treatment.

Conclusions

DED was associated with reduced agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace. Short-term ocular surface treatment was associated with improved measurement stability.

records.title: Biomechanical stiffening effect in ultra-high-fluence extracorporeal crosslinked corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segments.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Biomechanical stiffening effect in ultra-high-fluence extracorporeal crosslinked corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segments.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the biomechanical stiffening effects of a new ultra-high-fluence corneal crosslinking (CXL) protocol with conventional high-fluence CXL for extracorporeal corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segment optimization (ECO-CAIRS).

Setting

ELZA Institute, Zurich, Switzerland.

Design

Experimental, randomized, controlled, ex vivo laboratory study using porcine corneas. No masking was applied.

Methods

84 porcine corneas were divided into 4 groups: Group A (control), Group B (10 J/cm 2 ), Group C (30 J/cm 2 ), and Group D (60 J/cm 2 ). After epithelial debridement, Groups B, C, and D were treated with 0.1% hypo-osmolar riboflavin. UV-A irradiation was delivered at fluences of 10 J/cm 2 (18 mW/cm 2 , 9:15 min) for Group B, 30 J/cm 2 (30 mW/cm 2 , 16:40 min) for Group C, and 60 J/cm 2 (30 mW/cm 2 , 33:18 min) for Group D. Corneal biomechanical properties were assessed by stress‑strain extensiometry.

Results

Mean elastic modulus (5% strain) values were as follows: Group A (1.39 ± 0.49 N/mm), Group B (1.83 ± 0.48 N/mm), Group C (2.25 ± 0.83 N/mm), and Group D (2.31 ± 0.88 N/mm). Ultra-high-fluence groups (C and D) showed significantly greater stiffening than Group B ( P = .041 and P = .015), with no significant difference between Groups C and D ( P = 1.00). Group B exhibited significantly greater stiffening than Group A ( P = .023).

Conclusions

Ultra-high-fluence CXL enhances biomechanical stiffening compared with conventional high-fluence CXL, supporting its use in ECO-CAIRS. In this extracorporeal context, endothelial safety and haze are irrelevant, while increased stiffness facilitates intrastromal ring insertion and reduces corneal swelling.

records.title: Uncorrected Visual Acuity and Visual Function Difficulties After Implantation of Simultaneous Vision Intraocular Lenses.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Uncorrected Visual Acuity and Visual Function Difficulties After Implantation of Simultaneous Vision Intraocular Lenses.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the association between binocular uncorrected visual acuity (UVA) at different distances and patient-reported difficulty with individual VF-14 activities after implantation of simultaneous vision intraocular lenses (SVIOLs).

Setting

("Masked by journal requirement").

Design

Retrospective observational.

Methods

Twelve-month data from 276 subjects implanted with either a Full-DOFi Smooth or a Partial-DOFi Extended IOL were included in the analysis. Visual acuities were obtained for far (UDVA, 4 m), intermediate (UIVA, 66 cm), and near (UNVA, 40 cm) distances, along with responses to a validated Spanish version of the VF-14 administered without spectacles. VF-14 responses were dichotomized (little/no vs other), and logistic regression analyses were performed to examine their associations with UDVA, UIVA, and UNVA. Statistical cut-off values were explored using the Youden index.

Results

UDVA was significantly associated with "traffic signs" and "night driving" (p < 0.05), whereas "watching TV" showed p = 0.06. UNVA was significantly associated with "knitting" (p < 0.05), whereas "large print" showed p = 0.06, and UIVA was associated with "newspapers" (p = 0.02). "Small print" and "knitting" were associated with both UIVA and UNVA, whereas "filling out forms" was associated only with UNVA (p < 0.05). Visual acuities were not associated with the remaining VF-14 items. Exploratory cut-off values maximizing the Youden index were generally 0.1 logMAR, except for "large print" (0.3 logMAR) and "traffic signs" (0.2 logMAR).

Conclusions

Only some VF-14 items were associated with binocular UVA. These findings may inform the development of PRO instruments for evaluating functional differences among SVIOLs.

records.title: Alignment Between Corneal Biomechanical Anisotropy and Toricity Using Optical Coherence Elastography.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Alignment Between Corneal Biomechanical Anisotropy and Toricity Using Optical Coherence Elastography.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the agreement in orientation and magnitude between corneal toricity and biomechanical anisotropy using optical coherence elastography (OCE).

Setting

College of Optometry, University of Houston, Houston, Texas, USA.

Design

Prospective cross-sectional study.

Methods

Healthy participants with spherical refractive error or corneal astigmatism > 0.50D were included. Corneal radial mechanical wave propagation speed, a proxy for corneal shear modulus, was measured using air-pulse wave-based OCE imaging (30° intervals over 360°). Biomechanical principal meridian () was defined as meridian with greatest wave speed, and its magnitude was calculated as difference between principal and orthogonal meridians. Likewise, astigmatic principal meridian () was defined as steep corneal meridian from videokeratography, and its magnitude was defined as dioptric difference between orthogonal steep and flat meridians. To compare these different domains (biomechanical anisotropy and astigmatism) within and across subjects, both vector magnitudes were cohort-normalized. Directional alignment between and was assessed using polar double-angle plots. Vectorial difference between these measures quantified similarities in both orientation and magnitude.

Results

30 eyes from 30 subjects were studied. Corneal astigmatism ranged from 0.15 to 3.66D (1.4±0.8D; mean±SD). Corneal wave speed in steep meridian was faster (12.97±1.6m/s) compared to flat meridian(9.03±1.8m/s). Biomechanical anisotropy strongly correlated with astigmatism (R2 = 0.88). Angular difference between and was 6.0°±7.1° among astigmatic eyes. Cohort-normalized magnitude difference between and was 0.06±0.07.

Conclusions

In vivo human corneal wave-based OCE measurements demonstrate that corneal biomechanical anisotropy exhibits an orthogonal pattern, highly correlated in orientation and magnitude with corneal topography.

records.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
content.abstract: Posterior chamber phakic intraocular lenses have a strong short-to-medium-term safety profile on the modern central-port platform, and a 2025 US Food and Drug Administration expansion of the indicated age range for a central-port phakic IOL to 21 to 60 years widens the eligible population. These lenses are to remain in the eye for decades, yet the field has defined what to monitor without building the infrastructure to deliver that monitoring reliably as patients age, change providers, and relocate. Existing guidance specifies endothelial and vault thresholds but does not address who monitors after the implanting surgeon, how baseline and longitudinal data transfer, or how late events are learned across practices. We propose three measures: upgrading the implant identification card into a longitudinal, portable surveillance record; a risk-stratified, age-informed surveillance framework developed through multisociety consensus; and a prospective implant registry with a defined minimum dataset. The device's clinical maturation now requires a parallel evolution in its care model.

records.title: Treatment-induced changes in higher-order aberrations after ray-tracing-guided vs. wavefront-optimized laser in situ keratomileusis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Treatment-induced changes in higher-order aberrations after ray-tracing-guided vs. wavefront-optimized laser in situ keratomileusis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Intraindividual comparison of treatment-induced changes of ocular higher-order aberrations (HOAs) after ray-tracing-guided laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) and wavefront-optimized LASIK.

Setting

University hospital.

Design

Prospective, randomized, eye-to-eye comparative study.

Methods

Patients with myopia and myopic astigmatism underwent ray-tracing-guided wavelight plus (Alcon) LASIK in one eye and wavefront-optimized LASIK in the fellow eye. The study assessed treatment-induced changes (3 months postoperative - preoperative) in root-mean-square (RMS) of total HOAs, primary spherical aberration, RMS coma and RMS trefoil after wavelight plus and wavefront-optimized LASIK.

Results

Thirty patients (sixty eyes) were included in the study. The mean change (± standard deviation) in RMS of total HOAs at 6-mm zone of analysis was 0.00±0.15µm after wavelight plus (p=0.758) and 0.11±0.12µm after wavefront-optimized LASIK (p<0.001). A negative spherical aberration change of -0.07±0.13µm (p=0.012) occurred after wavelight plus and a positive change of 0.06±0.09µm (p<0.001) after wavefront-optimized treatment. Changes in coma and trefoil were 0.02±0.15µm (p=0.474) and -0.02±0.10µm (p=0.225) after wavelight plus, while after wavefront-optimized LASIK they were respectively, 0.10±0.13µm (p<0.001) and 0.02±0.06µm (p=0.058). In contralateral-eye comparison, wavelight plus resulted in lower total HOAs in all patients with elevated preoperative HOAs (RMS of total HOAs >0.30µm, n=13 patients) and in 70.6% of patients (n=12) with low preoperative HOAs (≤0.30µm, n=17 patients).

Conclusions

Wavefront-optimized LASIK increased total HOAs, spherical aberration and coma, while no increase in HOAs was detected after wavelight plus. Spherical aberration decreased (negative change) after wavelight plus. The benefit of ray-tracing-guided LASIK tended to be larger in patients with higher preoperative HOAs.

records.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the long-term visual, refractive, and patient-reported satisfaction of epithelial photorefractive keratectomy (ePRK) combined with corneal cross-linking (CXL) - the Tel-Aviv Protocol - in patients with progressive keratoconus.

Setting

Care-Vision Laser Center, Tel Aviv, Israel.

Design

Retrospective, single-center case series.

Methods

Consecutive patients with progressive keratoconus who underwent ePRK-CXL were included. Preoperative and last-available postoperative pachymetry, keratometry (Kmean, Kmin, Kmax), spherical equivalent (SEQ), manifest refraction, uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), and corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA) were recorded; safety and efficacy indices were calculated. Patient-reported outcomes regarding spectacle/contact lens dependence, satisfaction, and visual symptoms were assessed with a structured questionnaire.

Results

Fifty eyes of 38 patients (mean age 25.9±6.8 years) were followed for a mean of 2,910±605 days (∼8 years; range 5-12). UDVA improved from 1.04±0.70 to 0.36±0.37 logMAR and CDVA from 0.23±0.16 to 0.11±0.10 logMAR (both P < 0.001); safety and efficacy indices were 1.42±0.55 and 0.93±0.51. K-max decreased from 47.51±2.96 to 45.95±2.99 D and SEQ from -2.42±2.29 to -0.82±1.57 D (both P < 0.001). Pachymetry decreased from 448.65±38.95 to 418.93±55.77 μm. Overall satisfaction was high (81.6% satisfied/very satisfied), 76.3% reported subjective visual improvement, 52.6% achieved spectacle independence, and 92.1% required no contact lenses. No progression was observed in the examined eyes.

Conclusions

At a mean follow-up of ∼8 years, the Tel-Aviv Protocol provided durable visual and refractive improvement, stabilized keratometry without progression, and yielded high patient satisfaction with low symptom burden. These results support ePRK-CXL as a tissue-sparing option for progressive keratoconus.

records.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.

content.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.
content.abstract:
Importance

US ophthalmology residency programs are divided between traditional resident clinic-based models with a separate faculty practice, and universal practice-based models. Little data exist comparing these educational models.

Objective

To evaluate the association of changing a traditional resident clinic training model to a universal practice plus urgent eye clinic-based residency training model with sociodemographic disparities and resident education.

Design, setting, and participants

This was a cross-sectional study conducted at a US academic medical center. All patients presenting to the University of Rochester Flaum Eye Institute between the period July 1, 2017, to June 30, 2019, and the period July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2024, were divided into 4 cohorts for retrospective analysis as follows: resident clinic 2017-2019, faculty practice 2017-2019, urgent eye clinic 2022-2024, and universal practice 2022-2024.

Exposures

The resident clinic was transitioned to urgent eye clinic in July 2022. All former patients from resident clinic were reassigned to the new universal practice.

Main outcomes and measures

Patient cohorts were compared regarding insurance payor(s) and self-identified race. Level of disease acuity in resident clinic and urgent eye clinic were compared. Graduating resident procedural volumes were compared.

Results

Participants were divided into the following 4 cohorts: resident clinic 2017-2019 (6819 patients), faculty practice 2017-2019 (61 847 patients), urgent eye clinic 2022-2024 (5124 patients), and universal practice 2022-2024 (79 001 patients), for a total of 118 459 patients (mean [SD] age, 47 [25] years; 65 186 female [55%]). Pretransition, compared with faculty practice patients, greater proportions of resident clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (62.1% vs 19.4%; difference, 32.0%; 95% CI, 30.9%-33.1%; P < .001) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native (ie, American Indian or Alaska Native), or other (51.9% vs 23.6%; difference, 28.3%; 95% CI, 27.1%-29.5%; P < .001). Posttransition, compared with universal practice patients, similar proportions of urgent eye clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (26.8% vs 27.8%; difference, 0.4%; 95% CI, -0.7% to 1.6%; P = .42) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native, or other (29.6% vs 26.8%; difference, 2.8%; 95% CI, 1.5%-4.1%; P < .001). A greater proportion of urgent eye clinic patients presented with high-acuity disease (37.6%) compared with resident clinic patients (20.9%; difference, 16.7%; 95% CI, 15.0%-18.4%; P < .001). Median graduating resident primary cataract surgery volume increased from 148 to 228 cases (difference, 80; 95% CI, 49 to 122; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cross-sectionals study show that transforming resident clinic into urgent eye clinic was associated with reduced sociodemographic disparities, enhanced resident exposure to high-acuity disease, and increased resident procedural experience. These results suggest that changes in resident clinic structure may improve both health equity and resident education.

records.title: Standardising ocular surface photography for artificial intelligence: current limitations and a proposed roadmap.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Standardising ocular surface photography for artificial intelligence: current limitations and a proposed roadmap.
content.abstract: Slit-lamp colour photography remains a cornerstone of anterior segment documentation and longitudinal monitoring. However, conventional slit-lamp photography has seen relatively limited technological advancement compared with the rapid development of quantitative anterior-segment modalities such as AS-OCT, Scheimpflug tomography and confocal microscopy. Despite the wide diffusion of digital cameras, smartphones, and high-end slit-lamp systems, ocular surface photography (OSP) remains hampered by the absence of standardised acquisition and processing protocols. The convex, aspheric geometry of the ocular surface, off-axis illumination, peripheral defocus, automatic colour correction, and pupil-driven exposure variation in retroillumination limit reproducibility, inter-device comparability, and clinical utility. In this review we critically appraise current OSP applications across major ocular surface conditions (dry eye disease, conjunctival hyperaemia, infectious keratitis, ocular surface burns, and ocular surface neoplasia), mapping the hardware, software, and reproducibility limitations that constrain clinical practice. We then examine how these limitations propagate into artificial intelligence (AI) development, where the absence of large, well-annotated, demographically diverse OSP datasets, together with the lack of reproducible quantitative phenotypes and reliable labels, is now the principal bottleneck to clinically deployable models; we discuss patient-level data partitioning and external validation, and outline how deep learning, federated learning and foundation models can both utilise and improve OSP. Finally, we propose a minimum acquisition and dataset specification, tiered by clinical setting from research to community screening, and a staged roadmap that combines hardware standardisation (focus-stacked, illumination-controlled, colour-calibrated acquisition), interoperable metadata-rich storage (DICOM where infrastructure permits), quantitative phenotype definition, and diverse international dataset collaborations, so that the ocular surface can benefit from quantitative imaging and AI as other areas of ophthalmology have begun to.

records.title: Changing Patterns of Dry Eye Disease Management in Korea: A Nationwide 10-Year Analysis.

content.title: Changing Patterns of Dry Eye Disease Management in Korea: A Nationwide 10-Year Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate long-term trends in treated dry eye disease (DED) prevalence and medication prescribing patterns in Korea using a nationwide mandatory insurance claims database.

Design

Retrospective nationwide clinical cohort study.

Participants

Patients identified from the Korean NHIS mandatory claims database (2014-2023).

Methods

DED was defined by at least one relevant ICD-10 diagnosis code together with at least one prescription for a DED-related topical medication within the same calendar year. Annual overall, sex-specific, and age-specific prevalence was calculated using the corresponding mid-year resident population. Medication classes and single-use versus multi-use formulations were evaluated. Medication use in Sjögren syndrome-associated versus non-Sjögren DED was compared using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age and sex.

Main outcome measures

Annual treated DED prevalence, medication prescribing proportions, formulation-specific prescribing trends, and differences between Sjögren syndrome-associated and non-Sjögren syndrome DED.

Results

Approximately 61.8 million patient-years were analyzed, representing 9.87 million unique patients. Annual treated DED prevalence ranged from 4.84% to 5.61% and was consistently higher in women and older individuals. Hyaluronic acid (HA) remained the most prescribed medication, although its proportional share declined from 85.03% in 2014 to 76.89% in 2023 (P < .001). Diquafosol prescriptions increased from 4.61% to 10.77%, and cyclosporine prescriptions increased from 2.39% to 5.77% (both P < .001). Single-use HA prescriptions increased from 39.73% to 73.76% (P < .001), and single-use diquafosol accounted for 61.8% of diquafosol prescriptions by 2023. Cyclosporine was prescribed to 26.00% of patients with Sjögren syndrome-associated DED and 7.51% of those with non-Sjögren DED; the adjusted OR was 4.06 (95% CI, 3.99-4.12).

Conclusions

Over the past decade, DED management in Korea shifted toward the anti-inflammatory cyclosporine, the mucin and water secretagogue diquafosol, and preservative-free single-use formulations. Patients with Sjögren syndrome-associated DED demonstrated distinct prescribing patterns, including substantially greater cyclosporine use after adjustment for age and sex.

records.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.

content.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To prospectively validate the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS), a standardized slit-lamp grading tool, by evaluating associations with objective corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and visual acuity in a real-world cystinosis cohort.

Design

Prospective observational cross-sectional study.

Participants

Seventy patients (140 eyes) with confirmed cystinosis were examined at the 2024-2025 Cystinosis Research Foundation Day of Hope Clinics.

Methods

All eyes underwent live slit-lamp UCI CCCS grading (0-5). Pentacam Scheimpflug densitometry was obtained in 68 eyes. Two ophthalmologists independently graded patients during the 2025 clinic to assess inter-rater reliability. Patient-reported symptoms, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and topical cysteamine treatment data were collected. Linear mixed-effects models accounting for within-patient correlation were used for densitometry and BCVA analyses. Symptom associations were evaluated at the patient level using Kendall's tau-b.

Main outcome measures

Inter-rater reliability of UCI CCCS; associations with corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and BCVA.

Results

Inter-rater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.995; 95% CI, 0.992-0.996). Linear mixed-effects modeling demonstrated significant associations between UCI CCCS grade and central (p = 0.0016) and anterior corneal densitometry (p = 0.0011) after accounting for within-patient correlation between fellow eyes. Higher UCI CCCS grades were significantly associated with greater photophobia (τ = 0.397, p < 0.0001), foreign-body sensation (τ = 0.295, p = 0.0047), and ocular dryness (τ = 0.405, p = 0.0001). No statistically significant association was observed between UCI CCCS grade and BCVA after accounting for within-patient correlation (p = 0.4389). No significant differences in UCI CCCS or corneal densitometry were observed across topical cysteamine treatment groups.

Conclusion

The UCI CCCS is a highly reproducible, clinically practical grading tool associated with objective corneal densitometry and patient-reported symptom burden, while BCVA was not significantly associated with UCI CCCS grade. Longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate treatment responsiveness and prognostic value.

records.title: Comparison of refractive surgeries (SMILE, LASIK, and PRK) with and without corneal crosslinking: systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of refractive surgeries (SMILE, LASIK, and PRK) with and without corneal crosslinking: systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract: Corneal crosslinking (CXL) is used for treating keratoconus and post-laser in situ keratomileusis ectasia. However, refractive surgery is not usually performed with prophylactic CXL. Therefore, we performed a meta-analysis comparing outcomes of refractive surgeries with vs without prophylactic CXL. We systematically searched databases for studies comparing refractive surgeries for myopic correction with vs without prophylactic corneal crosslinking. Review Manager 5.4.1 was used to perform statistical analysis. We included 2820 eyes from 28 studies. Compared with refractive surgery alone, surgery with prophylactic CXL resulted in decreased central corneal thickness, corrected distance visual acuity logMAR, and safety and efficacy indices. There were no significant differences in postoperative uncorrected distance visual acuity of 20/20 or better at ≥12 months and other visual outcomes among both groups. More randomized controlled trials with standard crosslinking protocols are needed to analyze the prophylactic use of crosslinking with refractive surgeries.

records.title: Combined Accelerated Crosslinking With Laser In Situ Keratomileusis (LASIK) for Myopic Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Combined Accelerated Crosslinking With Laser In Situ Keratomileusis (LASIK) for Myopic Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) and Simultaneous LASIK and accelerated Crosslinking (LASIK Xtra) for myopia correction.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

A search of PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and China National Knowledge Internet was conducted up to October 1, 2024 to identify studies comparing LASIK and LASIK Xtra for myopia correction. The outcome of visual acuity and refraction, safety, efficiency, predictability, stability, postoperative corneal thickness and endothelial cell count were measure.

Results

A total of 1,647 eyes (836 LASIK, 811 LASIK Xtra) from 15 studies were included. LASIK demonstrated superior postoperative uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA) compared to LASIK Xtra, with a mean difference (MD) of -0.03 (8 studies, n = 750 eyes; 95% CI: -0.04 to -0.01, P = .007) at 1 month and (7 studies, n = 672 eyes; MD= -0.01 95% CI: -0.02 to 0.00, P = .02) for long-term results (≥6 months). No significant differences were found in corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA; 6 studies, n = 530 eyes; MD = 0.00, 95% CI: -0.01, 0.00, P = .32), spherical equivalent (14 studies, n = 1639 eyes; MD = 0.03, 95% CI: -0.03, 0.08; P = .40), safety (8 studies, n = 779 eyes; odds ratios [OR]= 0.70; 95% CI: 0.39, 1.26; P = .23), efficiency (11 studies, n = 921 eyes; OR = 0.75, 95% CI: 0.54, 1.05, P = .10), predictability (11 studies, n = 971 eyes; OR= 1.03, 95% CI: 0.72, 1.47, P = .86), stability (3 studies, n = 90 eyes; OR = 0.70, 95% CI: 0.21, 2.28, P = .55). Subgroup analysis indicated a higher risk of postoperative CDVA loss in the Ectasia Risk Group undergoing LASIK-Xtra (OR= 0.20, 95% CI: 0.04 to 0.97, P = .05). The 30 mW/cm² for 90 seconds (2.7 J/cm²) irradiation protocol in LASIK Xtra may resulted in worse UDVA compared to LASIK (MD= -0.01, 95% CI: -0.03 to -0.001, P = .05). The certainty of evidence for the outcomes ranged from "low to very low".

Conclusions

Current evidence suggests that LASIK offers a statistically significant advantage in UDVA compared to LASIK Xtra, especially when LASIK Xtra irradiation protocol of 30 mW/cm² for 90 seconds (2.7 J/cm²) is applied. However, given the low to very low certainty of evidence, these findings require cautious interpretation and further confirmation through long-term studies.

records.title: Patient-reported outcome measures after multifocal and extended depth of focus intraocular lens implantation in refractive lens exchange and cataract surgery.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Patient-reported outcome measures after multifocal and extended depth of focus intraocular lens implantation in refractive lens exchange and cataract surgery.
content.abstract: Presbyopia-correcting intraocular lenses (IOLs) represent a fast-growing segment of ophthalmic surgery. The evaluation of lens performance has undergone a fundamental shift: best-corrected visual acuity alone is an insufficient measure of the clinical benefit of premium IOLs, whose true value lies in spectacle independence, visual quality, and visual function in daily activities. In that regard, patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) are a cornerstone of presbyopia-correcting IOL assessment. This review provides an overview of the current landscape of IOLs, PROM instruments and their limitations, visual function outcomes across IOL types and comorbidities, and future directions. Higher near performance often comes at the cost of greater dysphotopsia, and no single IOL design dominates across all PROM domains. Optimal IOL selection or combination therefore requires identifying which PROM domain matters most to the individual patient. While not absolute contraindications, dry eye disease and prior refractive surgery are the strongest predictors of suboptimal outcomes and therefore warrant careful preoperative consideration. As visual demands increasingly shift toward near and intermediate distances with growing digital device use, clinicians and manufacturers must align IOL design priorities and patient selection with evolving patient needs. The visual function index (VF)-14 questionnaire and most other vision-specific PROM instruments were developed in a pre-digital era and require modernization to remain valid measures of patient success. In an aging active population, multifocal and extended depth of focus IOLs, when matched to the right patients, represent one of surgery's most impactful quality-of-life interventions.

records.title: Efficacy, safety, and predictability of transepithelial vs mechanical or alcohol-assisted photorefractive keratectomy: meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Efficacy, safety, and predictability of transepithelial vs mechanical or alcohol-assisted photorefractive keratectomy: meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

The aim of this study was to assess the meta-analysis of the studies comparing transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (transPRK) with classic photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) (mechanical or alcohol-assisted).

Clinical relevance

Although PRK is a well-established procedure, transPRK, a newer, minimally invasive technique may reduce surgery time and improve patient outcomes. Comparing these techniques helps optimize surgical choices.

Methods

Relevant studies were collected from PubMed and were included if they met the following criteria: comparison of transPRK and PRK in efficacy, safety, predictability, correction index, difference vector, or index of success. The odds ratio (OR) estimates, risk ratio, and 95% CIs were derived from random-effects meta-analysis.

Results

20 studies with a total of 10 204 treated eyes were included in this meta-analysis. The pooled estimates between transPRK and PRK were as follows: log(OR) of the efficacy had a value of 0 (CI -0.32 to 0.33), log(OR) of the safety was 0.04 (CI -0.98 to 1.06), and log(OR) of the predictability was 0.48 (CI 0.16-0.81).

Conclusions

This meta-analysis showed that there were no statistically significant differences in either of the visual outcomes (efficacy, efficacy index, safety, safety index, and predictability). Although transPRK is preferred for its minimally invasive approach and quicker recovery, PRK continues to be a reliable option, particularly in environments where advanced technology is not easily affordable. The choice of laser platform can also influence the surgical outcomes through features such as advanced pulse technology, optimized ablation speed, and profiles.

records.title: Safety and Efficacy of Posterior Chamber Phakic Implantable Collamer Lenses in Patients with Keratoconus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Safety and Efficacy of Posterior Chamber Phakic Implantable Collamer Lenses in Patients with Keratoconus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To assess the safety and efficacy of phakic implantable collamer lenses (ICLs) in patients with keratoconus.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

We conducted a pre- and postintervention single-arm systematic review and meta-analysis in line with guidelines from the Cochrane Collaboration and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 Consensus Statement. We searched five electronic databases and the grey literature for any studies evaluating ICLs in the setting of keratoconus. Our primary outcomes were the corrected distance visual acuity, uncorrected distance visual acuity, and manifest cylinder astigmatism. Secondary outcomes included uncorrected near visual acuity, spherical equivalent, refractive astigmatism, higher-order aberrations, endothelial cell density, intraocular pressure, and incidence of adverse events. We summarized our analyses by calculating standardized mean differences (SMDs) with associated 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using random-effects meta-analysis.

Results

Sixteen observational studies, totaling 397 eyes, were eligible. Postoperatively, there was no statistically significant improvement in corrected distance visual acuity (SMD: -0.97, 95% CI: -1.99 to 0.05, P < .06); there was a statistically significant improvement in uncorrected distance visual acuity (SMD: -5.41, 95% CI: -0.704 to -3.78, P < .05), manifest cylinder (SMD: 2.27, 95% CI: 1.83-2.70, P < .05), spherical equivalent (SMD: -4.66, 95% CI: -5.63 to 3.68, P < .05), and refractive astigmatism (SMD: 2.22, 95% CI: 1.03-3.41, P < .05). No significant adverse events occurred.

Conclusions

Use of ICLs in patients with keratoconus is safe and effective, resulting in significant improvements in a myriad of visual and refractive measures. Our results remain limited by the observational design of included studies as well as the limited follow-up duration.

records.title: A REVIEW OF FLUORESCEIN ANGIOGRAPHY, INDOCYANINE GREEN ANGIOGRAPHY, AND OTHER FLUOROPHORES IN OPHTHALMOLOGY.

content.title: A REVIEW OF FLUORESCEIN ANGIOGRAPHY, INDOCYANINE GREEN ANGIOGRAPHY, AND OTHER FLUOROPHORES IN OPHTHALMOLOGY.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To review fluorophores used in ophthalmology and summarize properties relevant to imaging, diagnosis, and safety.

Methods

Discussion of excitation, emission, and other essential properties of specific fluorophores.

Results

Sodium fluorescein, a fluorophore, is used for angiography and remains the cornerstone for retinal vascular imaging. Indocyanine green is also a fluorophore that absorbs light at longer wavelengths, enabling improved choroidal visualization and aiding in the diagnosis of various vascular, inflammatory, and neoplastic diseases. It is also used to stain the internal limiting membrane during vitreoretinal surgery. Other fluorophores, such as rose bengal, are used topically and can be used in the treatment of corneal fungal infections. Riboflavin has uses in the cornea, and curcurmin has potential uses because of its binding affinity to amyloid.

Conclusion

In addition to fluorescein and indocyanine green, there are expanding uses for additional fluorophores, with further investigation needed for new imaging and treatment techniques.

records.title: Comparison of Femtosecond Laser Assistance and Manual Trephination in Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty in the Treatment of Keratoconus: A Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Comparison of Femtosecond Laser Assistance and Manual Trephination in Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty in the Treatment of Keratoconus: A Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the efficacy and safety of femtosecond laser-assisted deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty (F-DALK) with those of manual-trephination DALK (M-DALK) in treating keratoconus.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

Through November 2022, we comprehensively searched PubMed, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, and 4 Chinese databases. Studies that involved comparisons between F-DALK and M-DALK groups and that reported on relevant efficacy and/or safety parameters were included. Primary outcomes were uncorrected- and corrected-distance visual acuity and intraoperative complication rates. Secondary outcomes were spherical equivalent, topographic astigmatism, refractive cylinder, mean keratometry, endothelial cell density, suture removal time, and postoperative complication rates. These data were analyzed using Cochrane Review Manager software version 5.3.

Results

This meta-analysis included 9 nonrandomized controlled studies involving 1713 eyes. In eyes treated with F-DALK, corrected-distance visual acuity at 1 to 6 months (weighted mean difference = -0.07 [95% confidence interval {CI} -0.10 to -0.03]; I2 = 0%; P < .001) after surgery was better and intraoperative Descemet membrane perforation occurred less often (odds ratio = 0.53 [95% CI 0.31-0.92]; I2 = 6%; P = .02) than in eyes treated with M-DALK. No clinically significant differences in other outcomes were found among the groups.

Conclusions

Both F-DALK and M-DALK are safe and efficacious for patients with keratoconus. Compared with M-DALK, F-DALK can provide better early visual acuity and reduce the intraoperative perforation rate, and its likely improvements to long-term visual quality and endothelial cell preservation warrant further investigation. In addition, the 2 techniques seem to be comparable regarding refractive outcomes and other complications.

records.title: Postoperative complication rates in intraocular lens placement and fixation methods for inadequate capsular bag support: review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Postoperative complication rates in intraocular lens placement and fixation methods for inadequate capsular bag support: review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

To evaluate the complication rates of different intraocular lens (IOL) placement methods in adults with inadequate capsular bag support.

Clinical relevance

The surgical correction of inadequate capsular bag support for the IOL harbors several challenges, and there is a wide range of surgical procedures.

Methods

For the purpose of this meta-analysis, surgical methods were grouped based on the location of IOL placement: (1) anterior chamber (AC) placement; (2) iris fixation, which included prepupillary or retropupillary placement of an iris-claw IOL, or iris suturing of an IOL; and (3) scleral fixation, which included scleral sutured and sutureless techniques. Only studies comparing the results of 2 or more different placement methods were analyzed. The study protocol has been registered in the PROSPERO database (CRD42023458557).

Results

15 studies were included in the final analysis, which reported results of 1247 eyes. The overall complication rate was nonsignificantly lower in iris fixation (4.4%; 95% CI, 3.6%-5.4%, P = .150) than in AC placement (7.4%; 95% CI, 6.4%-7.9%) and scleral fixation (7.4%; 95% CI, 6.5%-8.4%). Transient corneal edema was the most common complication in AC placement (29.9%; 95% CI, 2.4%-57.5%, P < .001), compared with scleral fixation (11.9%; 95% CI, 2.6%-21.2%) and iris fixation (4.1%; 95% CI, 0.8%-7.3%). Vitreous hemorrhages were more frequently reported after scleral fixation (8.5%; 95% CI, 6.3%-11.2%, P = .006) than in AC placement (5.4%; 95% CI, 3.4%-8.5%) and iris fixation (1.4%; 95% CI, 0.4%-4.2%), and so was IOL decentration/dislocation (8.9%; 95% CI, 6.7%-11.8%, P = .047 compared with 1.1%; 95% CI, 0.4%-3.4% and 4.0%; 95% CI, 2.2%-7.3%, respectively).

Conclusions

The risks associated with particular techniques should be taken into account in preoperative counseling and planning postoperative treatment.

records.title: TFOS DEWS III: Diagnostic Methodology.

content.title: TFOS DEWS III: Diagnostic Methodology.
content.abstract: A standard approach to the diagnosis of dry eye disease across eye care practitioners is critical to reassuring the patient, providing consistency between practitioners and informing governments as to the true prevalence and resulting healthcare needs. The Tear Film & Ocular Surface Society (TFOS) Dry Eye Workshop (DEWS) III has reviewed the evidence-base since their previous reports published in 2017 and revised the definition to "Dry eye is a multifactorial, symptomatic disease characterized by a loss of homeostasis of the tear film and/or ocular surface, in which tear film instability and hyperosmolarity, ocular surface inflammation and damage, and neurosensory abnormalities are etiological factors." Key features from the definition include that dry eye disease is multifactorial, is a disease and not a syndrome and is always symptomatic. Differential diagnosis and ocular examination guidance is given along with the risk factors that should be discussed with the patient. The recommended screening questionnaire is the OSDI-6 with a cut-off score ≥4. A positive result together with a non-invasive breakup time <10s or alternatively tear film hyperosmolarity (≥308mOsm/L in either eye or an interocular difference >8mOsm/L) or alternatively >5 corneal fluorescein and/or >9 conjunctival lissamine green punctate spots and/or lid margin lissamine green staining of ≥2mm length & ≥25 % width, gives a diagnosis of dry eye. Subclassification was separated into tear film deficiencies (lipid, aqueous and mucin/glycocalyx), eyelid anomalies (blink/lid closure and lid margin) and ocular surface abnormalities (anatomical misalignment, neural dysfunction, ocular surface cell damage/disruption and primary inflammation/oxidative stress) components, with appropriate clinical tests and cut-offs provided to identify these etiological drivers in an individual, to inform appropriate management and therapy.

records.title: Ocular changes in human spaceflight.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Ocular changes in human spaceflight.
content.abstract: Spaceflight presents unique challenges to ocular health, with astronauts experiencing a range of visual disturbances in the setting of microgravity, radiation exposure, and other environmental factors. This review synthesizes knowledge about how spaceflight affects ocular anatomy and function. We outline the diagnostic and therapeutic limitations in microgravity, including constraints on imaging modalities, intracranial pressure measurement, and drug delivery. In addition, we examine common spaceflight-associated ocular pathologies, including spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome, corneal epithelial disruption, possible radiation-associated lens changes, and retinal or choroidal alterations. Drawing from evidence across human missions, terrestrial analogs, and experimental models, this review emphasizes the critical importance of vision to astronaut safety and mission success. Future directions include long-term ocular health monitoring, advancement of in-flight diagnostic capabilities, and multidisciplinary strategies to safeguard astronaut vision.

records.title: Intraoperative Aberrometry versus Preoperative Biometry for Intraocular Lens Power Calculations: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Intraoperative Aberrometry versus Preoperative Biometry for Intraocular Lens Power Calculations: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the published literature to compare intraoperative aberrometry (IA) with preoperative biometry-based formulas with respect to intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation accuracy for various clinical scenarios.

Methods

Literature searches in the PubMed database conducted in August 2022, July 2023, and February 2024 identified 157, 18, and 6 citations, respectively. These were reviewed in abstract form, and 61 articles were selected for full-text review. Of these, 29 met the criteria for inclusion in this assessment. The panel methodologists assigned a level of evidence rating to each of the articles; 4 were rated level I, 19 were rated level II, and 6 were rated level III.

Results

Intraoperative aberrometry performed better than traditional vergence formulas, including the Haigis, HofferQ, Holladay, and SRK/T, and similarly to the Barrett Universal II and Hill-RBF with respect to minimization of spherical equivalent (SE) refractive error. For toric IOLs, IA outperformed formulas that only considered anterior corneal astigmatism and was similar to formulas like the Barrett Toric Calculator (BTC), which empirically account for the contribution from the posterior cornea. In eyes with a history of corneal refractive surgery, IA performed similarly to the Barrett True-K and slightly better than other tested methods, including the Haigis-L, Shammas, and Wang-Koch-Maloney formulas.

Conclusions

Intraoperative aberrometry corresponds well with modern vergence formulas, including the Barrett Universal II, Hill-RBF, BTC, and Barrett True-K. It has greater accuracy than traditional vergence-based IOL power calculation formulas in eyes with and without a history of corneal refractive surgery.

records.title: The pre-Descemet's layer (Dua's layer, also known as the Dua-Fine layer and the pre-posterior limiting lamina layer): Discovery, characterisation, clinical and surgical applications, and the controversy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The pre-Descemet's layer (Dua's layer, also known as the Dua-Fine layer and the pre-posterior limiting lamina layer): Discovery, characterisation, clinical and surgical applications, and the controversy.
content.abstract: The pre-Descemet's layer/Dua's layer, also termed the Dua-Fine layer and the pre-posterior limiting lamina layer, lies anterior to the Descemet's membrane in the cornea, is 10 μm (range 6-16) thick, made predominantly of type I and some type VI collagen with abundant elastin, more than any other layer of the cornea. It has high tensile strength (bursting pressure up to 700 mm of Hg), is impervious to air and almost acellular. At the periphery it demonstrates fenestrations and ramifies to become the core of the trabecular meshwork, with implications for intraocular pressure and glaucoma. It has been demonstrated in some species of animals. The layer has assumed considerable importance in anterior and posterior lamellar corneal transplant surgery by improving our understanding of the behaviour of corneal tissue during these procedures, improved techniques and made the surgery safer with better outcomes. It has led to the innovation of new surgical procedures namely, pre-Descemet's endothelial keratoplasty, suture management of acute hydrops, DALK-triple and Fogla's mini DALK. The discovery and knowledge of the layer has introduced paradigm shifts in our age old concepts of Descemet's membrane detachment, acute corneal hydrops in keratoconus and Descemetoceles, with impact on management approaches. It has been shown to contribute to the pathology and clinical signs observed in corneal infections and some corneal dystrophies. Early evidence suggests that it may have a role in the pathogenesis of keratoconus in relation to its elastin content. Its contribution to corneal biomechanics and glaucoma are subjects of current investigations.

records.title: Introducing the blood-tear barrier: Structure, function, and disruption in ocular surface homeostasis.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Introducing the blood-tear barrier: Structure, function, and disruption in ocular surface homeostasis.
content.abstract: Tear fluid exhibits a unique molecular composition distinct from blood, suggesting the presence of a selective blood-tear barrier (BTB) that regulates molecular exchange between ocular vasculature and the tear film. Although sporadically mentioned in the literature, the structure, functional roles, and mechanisms of disruption of this barrier have not yet been characterized. Based on current evidence, this review proposes a conceptual model in which the BTB comprises three successive compartments: the tear film, the epithelial layer, and the vascular endothelium, with tight junctions playing a central role in maintaining barrier integrity. The BTB appears to play a bidirectional protective role at the ocular surface, shielding the eye from external exposure while preventing the entry of blood-derived factors. This protective function is supported by literature describing interactions with microorganisms, blood-derived factors, drugs, and environmental factors. Similar to other physiological barriers in the body, the BTB is likely susceptible to disruption or breakdown. Potential disruptors include ocular surgery, topical or systemic drugs, contact lens wear, ocular surface diseases, and systemic conditions. Understanding the structure, functional roles, and mechanisms of disruption of the BTB is essential for maintaining ocular surface health and advancing the understanding of ocular surface disease.

records.title: Efficacy of a new water-free topical cyclosporine 0.1% solution for optimizing the ocular surface in patients with dry eye and cataract.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Efficacy of a new water-free topical cyclosporine 0.1% solution for optimizing the ocular surface in patients with dry eye and cataract.
content.abstract: This is a pooled analysis from 2 phase III clinical trials investigating a water-free topical cyclosporine 0.1% for the treatment of moderate to severe dry eye. The analyses included 1162 patients: 35% with cataract, 20% with pseudophakia, and 45% without cataract. Demographics or baseline characteristics were comparable across groups except for age and vision. The cyclosporine-treated patients achieved large mean improvements from baseline by day 15: -3.7 in patients without cataract, -3.2 in patients with cataract, and -3.1 in pseudophakic patients. These improvements were statistically significantly higher compared with the respective vehicle groups. In the cataract subgroup, 59% of patients treated with cyclosporine achieved ≥3 grade improvements in corneal staining score, as early as day 15. The magnitude of the effect and early onset of action make this new cyclosporine solution a promising candidate for preoperative management of ocular surface in patients undergoing cataract surgery.

records.title: Safety and Efficacy of Epithelium-Off Corneal Collagen Cross-Linking for the Treatment of Corneal Ectasia: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Safety and Efficacy of Epithelium-Off Corneal Collagen Cross-Linking for the Treatment of Corneal Ectasia: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To review the evidence on the safety and effectiveness of epithelium-off corneal collagen cross-linking (CXL) for the treatment of progressive corneal ectasia.

Methods

A literature search of the PubMed database was most recently conducted in March 2024 with no date restrictions and limited to studies published in English. The search identified 359 citations that were reviewed in abstract form, and 43 of these were reviewed in full text. High-quality randomized clinical trials comparing epithelium-off CXL with conservative treatment in patients who have keratoconus (KCN) and post-refractive surgery ectasia were included. The panel deemed 6 articles to be of sufficient relevance for inclusion, and these were assessed for quality by the panel methodologist; 5 were rated level I, and 1 was rated level II. There were no level III studies.

Results

This analysis includes 6 prospective, randomized controlled trials that evaluated the use of epithelium-off CXL to treat progressive KCN (5 studies) and post-laser refractive surgery ectasia (1 study), with a mean postoperative follow-up of 2.4 years (range, 1-5 years). All studies showed a decreased progression rate in treated patients compared with controls. Improvement in the maximum keratometry (Kmax) value, corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA), and uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA) was observed in the treatment groups compared with control groups. A decrease in corneal thickness was observed in both groups but was greater in the CXL group. Complications were rare.

Conclusions

Epithelium-off CXL is effective in reducing the progression of KCN and post-laser refractive surgery ectasia in most treated patients with an acceptable safety profile.

records.title: Healing the cornea: Exploring the therapeutic solutions offered by MSCs and MSC-derived EVs.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Healing the cornea: Exploring the therapeutic solutions offered by MSCs and MSC-derived EVs.
content.abstract: Affecting a large proportion of the population worldwide, corneal disorders constitute a concerning health hazard associated to compromised eyesight or blindness for most severe cases. In the last decades, mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) demonstrated promising abilities in improving symptoms associated to corneal diseases or alleviating these affections, especially through their anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory and pro-regenerative properties. More recently, MSC therapeutic potential was shown to be mediated by the molecules they release, and particularly by their extracellular vesicles (EVs; MSC-EVs). Consequently, using MSC-EVs emerged as a pioneering strategy to mitigate the risks related to cell therapy while providing MSC therapeutic benefits. Despite the promises given by MSC- and MSC-EV-based approaches, many improvements are considered to optimize the therapeutic significance of these therapies. This review aspires to provide a comprehensive and detailed overview of current knowledge on corneal therapies involving MSCs and MSC-EVs, the strategies currently under evaluation, and the gaps remaining to be addressed for clinical implementation. From encapsulating MSCs or their EVs into biomaterials to enhance the ocular retention time to loading MSC-EVs with therapeutic drugs, a wide range of ground-breaking strategies are currently contemplated to lead to the safest and most effective treatments. Promising research initiatives also include diverse gene therapies and the targeting of specific cell types through the modification of the EV surface, paving the way for future therapeutic innovations. As one of the most important challenges, MSC-EV large-scale production strategies are extensively investigated and offer a wide array of possibilities to meet the needs of clinical applications.

records.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.

content.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.
content.abstract:
Importance

Gene expression profiling (GEP) reliably predicts metastatic uveal melanoma risk and is used to manage uveal melanoma (UM) in patients with this diagnosis. Efforts to refine molecular prognostication continue.

Objective

To determine if confirmatory cytopathology findings influence the prognostic accuracy of a commercially available GEP/Preferentially Expressed Antigen in Melanoma (PRAME) assay.

Design, setting, and participants

The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group 2 study, a prospective cohort study, was conducted from 2017 to 2020 with follow-up recorded at 6-month intervals. This was a multicenter study that included patients with choroidal and/or ciliary body melanoma and results from a 15-GEP and PRAME RNA expression (15-GEP/PRAME) assay. Patients with iris tumors or less than 6 months' follow-up were excluded. Study data were analyzed from April 2025 to July 2026.

Exposures

15-GEP/PRAME, cytopathology, and next-generation sequencing (NGS).

Main outcomes and measures

Metastatic uveal melanoma rates in patients who had 15-GEP/PRAME and confirmatory cytopathology (CCP) results confirming or suspicious for UM (GEP+CCP) were compared with those who had 15-GEP/PRAME and no cytopathology performed, or unknown or nondiagnostic cytopathology results (GEP only). UM-associated variants identified by NGS were also evaluated.

Results

Of 1537 patients (mean [SD] age, 62.0 [13.4] years; 787 male [51.2%]), 727 (47.3%) had CCP results, and 810 (52.7%) had nondiagnostic cytopathology results or no cytopathology performed. Class 2/PRAME+ tumors were more common (136 of 727 [18.7%]) in the GEP+CCP group than in the GEP-only group (72 of 810 [8.9%]; 9.8% difference; 95% CI, 6.4-13.3; P <.001), whereas class 1/PRAME- tumors were less common (330 of 727 [45.4%] vs 495 of 810 [61.1%]; 15.7% difference; 95% CI, 10.8-20.6; P <.001). In patients with GEP+CCP, 22.7% (n = 165) developed metastasis vs 15.4% (n = 125) in patients with GEP only (7.3% difference, 95% CI, 3.3-11.2; P < .001). Adjusting for 15-GEP/PRAME status, there were no differences in metastasis rates between CCP groups. Of 1327 patients with successful NGS, 94.1% (605 of 643) in the GEP+CCP group and 71.9% (492 of 684) in the GEP-only group had a UM-associated variant (22.2% difference, 95% CI, 18.3-26.0; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cohort study reveal that no differences in metastasis outcomes were observed between patients with and without CCP within any GEP/PRAME categories. UM-associated variants were found less frequently in the GEP-only group than in the GEP+CCP group. In this cohort, 15-GEP/PRAME classification without CCP retained prognostic validity, supporting its clinical consideration in guiding metastatic surveillance in cases in which cytopathology is unavailable.

records.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.

content.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Investigate the structure-function relationships between epiretinal membrane (ERM) stage, tractional abnormalities, and the gap area between the ERM and the retinal surface, in relation to visual acuity and quantitative contrast sensitivity function in patients with idiopathic epiretinal membrane.

Methods

This was a retrospective, cross-sectional study involving 111 participants diagnosed with idiopathic ERM. All patients underwent a comprehensive ophthalmologic examination, spectral-domain optical coherence tomography imaging using the SPECTRALIS Heidelberg system, and contrast sensitivity (CS) testing using the quantitative contrast sensitivity function method.

Results

Progressive stages of ERM were associated with declines in both CS and visual acuity (β* = -0.45 to -0.19, P < 0.02), with CS showing a more pronounced reduction than visual acuity, especially between controls and Stage 1. Ectopic inner foveal layer thickness exhibited a similar pattern of decline in both visual acuity (β* = 0.42, P < 0.001) and CS (β* = -0.46 to -0.18, all P < 0.02). By contrast, SUKIMA showed no significant association with any of the visual measurements assessed. Among the tractional abnormalities, the cotton ball sign correlated with diminished vision, particularly reflected by a notable drop in CS at the highest spatial frequencies tested with reduced CS at 12 cycles per degree (β* = -0.44, P = 0.02) and 18 cycles per degree (β* = -0.46, P = 0.02).

Conclusion

Quantitative contrast sensitivity function testing is particularly important for assessing visual function in ERM development, especially in the early stages.

records.title: AI-ASSISTED OCT BIOMARKER QUANTIFICATION REVEALS DISTINCT RETINAL FLUID TRAJECTORIES IN CENTRAL RETINAL VEIN OCCLUSION.

content.title: AI-ASSISTED OCT BIOMARKER QUANTIFICATION REVEALS DISTINCT RETINAL FLUID TRAJECTORIES IN CENTRAL RETINAL VEIN OCCLUSION.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize longitudinal patterns of intraretinal (IRF) and subretinal fluid (SRF) dynamics using artificial intelligence-assisted optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarker quantification and to evaluate their association with long-term visual outcomes in eyes with central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO).

Methods

Patients with previously treatment-naïve CRVO and a documented 24-month follow-up were retrospectively included. All eyes received intravitreal aflibercept administered according to a treat-and-extend protocol. Spectral-domain OCT scans were analyzed at baseline and after 3 and 24 months. IRF and SRF volumes were quantified using RetinAI Discovery OCT Biomarker Detector (Ikerian AG). Linear regression models were used to assess the association between fluid volumes and 24-month corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA). Patients were clustered according to their IRF trajectories over time to identify distinct fluid-response phenotypes.

Results

Out of 173 patients, 64 eyes (64 patients) were included. Baseline IRF and SRF volumes showed no significant association with 24-month CDVA. Cluster analysis of longitudinal IRF trajectories identified four distinct fluid-response patterns. Eyes with low or rapidly resolving IRF achieved the best long-term visual outcomes (median CDVA 73 letters), whereas those with persistent or recurrent IRF showed poorer outcomes (median 53 letters; P = 0.008). Early IRF resolution tended to predict superior visual recovery at 24 months.

Conclusion

Artificial intelligence-based volumetric OCT analysis suggests that distinct retinal fluid trajectories in CRVO may have prognostic implications for long-term visual acuity, although these findings are preliminary and require validation. Dynamic IRF resolution patterns may be more informative than static fluid volumes for predicting functional outcomes after anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy.

records.title: Association of Retinal Microvascular Density with Hemodynamic and Clinical Severity Markers in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.

content.title: Association of Retinal Microvascular Density with Hemodynamic and Clinical Severity Markers in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate whether quantitative retinal microvascular and structural parameters, measured by optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), are associated with disease severity and right ventriculo-arterial coupling in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 45 patients with confirmed PAH, stratified by New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class (I-III). Patients with coexisting ocular pathologies were strictly excluded. Vessel density (VD) in the superficial (SCP) and deep capillary plexuses (DCP), foveal avascular zone characteristics, and ganglion cell complex (GCC) thickness were analyzed. These parameters were correlated with functional capacity (6-minute walk test [6-mWT]), NT-proBNP levels, and the echocardiographic TAPSE/sPAP ratio.

Results

Retinal VD in both SCP and DCP progressively decreased with worsening NYHA functional class (p < 0.05). Retinal VD showed a significant negative correlation with NT-proBNP levels (r = -0.355, p = 0.017) and a positive correlation with 6-mWT distance (r = 0.499, p < 0.001). Crucially, retinal microvascular density demonstrated a robust positive correlation with the TAPSE/sPAP ratio (r = 0.420, p = 0.004), a surrogate for right ventriculo-arterial coupling. GCC thickness exhibited variations across NYHA classes but lacked a consistent linear progression.

Conclusion

Retinal microvascular attenuation in PAH is strongly associated not only with functional and biochemical severity but also with central hemodynamic impairment represented by the TAPSE/sPAP ratio. These findings suggest that OCTA-derived vessel density may serve as a promising, non-invasive biomarker for monitoring systemic microvascular compromise and right heart function in PAH.

records.title: Glaucoma Genetic Risk Scores in the Million Veteran Program.

content.title: Glaucoma Genetic Risk Scores in the Million Veteran Program.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a degenerative eye disease for which early treatment is critical to mitigate visual impairment and irreversible blindness. POAG-associated loci individually confer incremental risk. Genetic risk score(s) (GRS) could enable POAG risk stratification. Despite significantly higher POAG burden among individuals of African ancestry (AFR), GRS are limited in this population. A recent large-scale, multi-ancestry meta-analysis identified 127 POAG-associated loci and calculated cross-ancestry and ancestry-specific effect estimates, including in European ancestry (EUR) and AFR individuals. We assessed the utility of the 127-variant GRS for POAG risk stratification in EUR and AFR Veterans in the Million Veteran Program (MVP). We also explored the association between GRS and documented invasive glaucoma surgery (IGS).

Design

Cross-sectional study.

Participants

MVP Veterans with imputed genetic data, including 5830 POAG cases (445 with IGS documented in the electronic health record) and 64 476 controls.

Methods

We tested unweighted and weighted GRS of 127 published risk variants in EUR (3382 cases and 58 811 controls) and AFR (2448 cases and 5665 controls) Veterans in the MVP. Weighted GRS were calculated using effect estimates from the most recently published report of cross-ancestry and ancestry-specific meta-analyses. We also evaluated GRS in POAG cases with documented IGS.

Main outcome measures

Performance of 127-variant GRS in EUR and AFR Veterans for POAG risk stratification and association with documented IGS.

Results

GRS were significantly associated with POAG (P < 5 × 10-5) in both groups; a higher proportion of EUR compared with AFR were consistently categorized in the top GRS decile (21.9%-23.6% and 12.9%-14.5%, respectively). Only GRS weighted by ancestry-specific effect estimates were associated with IGS documentation in AFR cases; all GRS types were associated with IGS in EUR cases.

Conclusions

Varied performance of the GRS for POAG risk stratification and documented IGS association in EUR and AFR Veterans highlights (1) the complex risk architecture of POAG, (2) the importance of diverse representation in genomics studies that inform GRS construction and evaluation, and (3) the necessity of expanding diverse POAG-related genomic data so that GRS can equitably aid in screening individuals at high risk of POAG and who may require more aggressive treatment.

records.title: Structure and function of ABCA4 and its role in the visual cycle and Stargardt macular degeneration.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Structure and function of ABCA4 and its role in the visual cycle and Stargardt macular degeneration.
content.abstract: ABCA4 is a member of the superfamily of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters that is preferentially localized along the rim region of rod and cone photoreceptor outer segment disc membranes. It uses the energy from ATP binding and hydrolysis to transport N-retinylidene-phosphatidylethanolamine (N-Ret-PE), the Schiff base adduct of retinal and phosphatidylethanolamine, from the lumen to the cytoplasmic leaflet of disc membranes. This ensures that all-trans-retinal and excess 11-cis-retinal are efficiently cleared from photoreceptor cells thereby preventing the accumulation of toxic retinoid compounds. Loss-of-function mutations in the gene encoding ABCA4 cause autosomal recessive Stargardt macular degeneration, also known as Stargardt disease (STGD1), and related autosomal recessive retinopathies characterized by impaired central vision and an accumulation of lipofuscin and bis-retinoid compounds. High resolution structures of ABCA4 in its substrate and nucleotide free state and containing bound N-Ret-PE or ATP have been determined by cryo-electron microscopy providing insight into the molecular architecture of ABCA4 and mechanisms underlying substrate recognition and conformational changes induced by ATP binding. The expression and functional characterization of a large number of disease-causing missense ABCA4 variants have been determined. These studies have shed light into the molecular mechanisms underlying Stargardt disease and a classification that reliably predicts the effect of a specific missense mutation on the severity of the disease. They also provide a framework for developing rational therapeutic treatments for ABCA4-associated diseases.

records.title: The impact of sensory neuropathy and inflammation on epithelial wound healing in diabetic corneas.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The impact of sensory neuropathy and inflammation on epithelial wound healing in diabetic corneas.
content.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is the most common complication of diabetes, with several underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, some of which are still uncertain. The cornea is an avascular tissue and sensitive to hyperglycemia, resulting in several diabetic corneal complications including delayed epithelial wound healing, recurrent erosions, neuropathy, loss of sensitivity, and tear film changes. The manifestation of DPN in the cornea is referred to as diabetic neurotrophic keratopathy (DNK). Recent studies have revealed that disturbed epithelial-neural-immune cell interactions are a major cause of DNK. The epithelium is supplied by a dense network of sensory nerve endings and dendritic cell processes, and it secretes growth/neurotrophic factors and cytokines to nourish these neighboring cells. In turn, sensory nerve endings release neuropeptides to suppress inflammation and promote epithelial wound healing, while resident immune cells provide neurotrophic and growth factors to support neuronal and epithelial cells, respectively. Diabetes greatly perturbs these interdependencies, resulting in suppressed epithelial proliferation, sensory neuropathy, and a decreased density of dendritic cells. Clinically, this results in a markedly delayed wound healing and impaired sensory nerve regeneration in response to insult and injury. Current treatments for DPN and DNK largely focus on managing the severe complications of the disease. Cell-based therapies hold promise for providing more effective treatment for diabetic keratopathy and corneal ulcers.

records.title: Trustworthy AI: Closing the gap between development and integration of AI systems in ophthalmic practice.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Trustworthy AI: Closing the gap between development and integration of AI systems in ophthalmic practice.
content.abstract: An increasing number of artificial intelligence (AI) systems are being proposed in ophthalmology, motivated by the variety and amount of clinical and imaging data, as well as their potential benefits at the different stages of patient care. Despite achieving close or even superior performance to that of experts, there is a critical gap between development and integration of AI systems in ophthalmic practice. This work focuses on the importance of trustworthy AI to close that gap. We identify the main aspects or challenges that need to be considered along the AI design pipeline so as to generate systems that meet the requirements to be deemed trustworthy, including those concerning accuracy, resiliency, reliability, safety, and accountability.
