We elaborate on mechanisms and considerations to address those aspects or challenges, and define the roles and responsibilities of the different stakeholders involved in AI for ophthalmic care, i.e., AI developers, reading centers, healthcare providers, healthcare institutions, ophthalmological societies and working groups or committees, patients, regulatory bodies, and payers. Generating trustworthy AI is not a responsibility of a sole stakeholder. There is an impending necessity for a collaborative approach where the different stakeholders are represented along the AI design pipeline, from the definition of the intended use to post-market surveillance after regulatory approval. This work contributes to establish such multi-stakeholder interaction and the main action points to be taken so that the potential benefits of AI reach real-world ophthalmic settings.

records.title: A CONSENSUS ON RISK MITIGATION FOR BROLUCIZUMAB IN NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: Patient Selection, Evaluation, and Treatment.

content.title: A CONSENSUS ON RISK MITIGATION FOR BROLUCIZUMAB IN NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: Patient Selection, Evaluation, and Treatment.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Brolucizumab has high efficacy in retinal fluid resolution and provides the possibility for longer dosing intervals in the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration. However, brolucizumab has been associated with events of retinal vasculitis and retinal vascular occlusion typically in the presence of other signs of intraocular inflammation (IOI). The purpose of this report is to provide guidance on the use of brolucizumab for neovascular age-related macular degeneration to a global audience.

Methods

A literature review was conducted on adverse events related to IOI after administration of brolucizumab in eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

Results

Possible risk factors for IOI and retinal vascular occlusion after brolucizumab should be considered before administering brolucizumab. Patients who receive brolucizumab should be educated on the symptoms, signs, and time course of IOI after brolucizumab. Before each injection of brolucizumab, physicians should assess the eye for any signs of inflammation and not treat with brolucizumab if inflammation is detected. Treatment of IOI should be prompt and provided with particular attention to the posterior segment.

Conclusion

Careful patient selection, patient education, assessment for inflammation, and intensive treatment of possible inflammation are important when using brolucizumab in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

records.title: Topical Pharmacologic Interventions Versus Active Control, Placebo, or No Treatment for Epidemic Keratoconjunctivitis: Findings From a Cochrane Systematic Review.

content.title: Topical Pharmacologic Interventions Versus Active Control, Placebo, or No Treatment for Epidemic Keratoconjunctivitis: Findings From a Cochrane Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To summarize key findings from a Cochrane systematic review of the effectiveness and safety of topical pharmacologic interventions compared with active control or placebo for epidemic keratoconjunctivitis (EKC).

Design

Systematic review.

Methods

We included randomized controlled trials that compared antiseptic agents, virustatic agents, or immune-modulating topical therapies with placebo or an active control. We adhered to Cochrane methods for trial selection, data extraction, risk of bias evaluation, and data synthesis.

Results

Ten randomized controlled trials with 892 participants with acute or chronic EKC were included. Eight trials compared interventions with artificial tears or saline (n = 4) or with steroids (n = 4); two 3-arm trials contributed data to both comparisons. Estimates suggested that compared with tears, after povidone-iodine (PVP-I) alone (2 studies, 409 participants) more participants with acute EKC had resolution of symptoms (risk ratio [RR] 1.15 [95% confidence interval {CI} 1.07-1.24]) and signs (RR 3.19 [95% CI 2.29-4.45]) within 10 days. In 2 trials comparing treatments with steroid alone or steroid with levofloxacin, fewer eyes treated with PVP-I or polyvinyl alcohol iodine (PVA-I) plus steroid developed subepithelial infiltrates within 21 days (RR 0.08 [95% CI 0.01-0.55]; 69 eyes). No treatment was shown to improve resolution of infiltrates.

Conclusions

Low- to very low-level certainty of evidence suggested that PVP-I or PVA-I with steroid may confer some benefit in acute EKC, but imprecision from small sample sizes, the potential risk of bias from inadequate reporting or trial design, and variability in participant selection, outcome measurement, and reporting limit the amount and quality of evidence.

records.title: INVERTED INTERNAL LIMITING MEMBRANE FLAP TECHNIQUE FOR MACULAR HOLE COEXISTENT WITH RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT.

content.title: INVERTED INTERNAL LIMITING MEMBRANE FLAP TECHNIQUE FOR MACULAR HOLE COEXISTENT WITH RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To report the clinical features and treatment outcomes of patients with macular hole coexistent with rhegmatogenous retinal detachment surgically treated with pars plana vitrectomy and inverted internal limiting membrane flap technique.

Methods

Eleven consecutive patients with rhegmatogenous retinal detachment and macular hole who underwent vitrectomy and internal limiting membrane peeling with the inverted flap technique between December 2017 and February 2021 were retrospectively evaluated. The main outcome measures were retinal reattachment rate, macular hole closure rate, and postoperative best-corrected visual acuity. A nonsystematic literature review was performed to compare the study outcomes with those previously reported.

Results

The primary retinal reattachment rate was 90% (10/11) with one surgery and 100% with 2 surgical procedures. Macular hole closure was achieved in all patients (11/11). All patients showed an improvement in visual acuity at the final postoperative visit, and the mean postoperative best-corrected visual acuity was 0.60 ± 0.32 logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution (20/80 Snellen equivalent).

Conclusion

Vitrectomy with the inverted internal limiting membrane flap technique achieved not only favorable anatomical retinal reattachment rates but also an encouraging recovery of central macular anatomy and visual function in patients with macular hole coexistent with rhegmatogenous retinal detachment.

records.title: What Are the Dry Eye Questionnaires Available in the Scientific Literature Used for? A Scoping Review.

content.title: What Are the Dry Eye Questionnaires Available in the Scientific Literature Used for? A Scoping Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Dry eye disease (DED) is a frequent chronic ophthalmic condition. Its diagnosis includes tests and patient reported outcomes (PRO) questionnaires. Although many PRO dry eye questionnaires (PRO-DEQs) are available, they differ greatly from each other and not all have been validated. The purpose of this study was to retrieve the PRO-DEQs present in the scientific literature by performing a descriptive analysis of them and identifying those with known validity and reliability characteristics and to perform a descriptive analysis of the geographic area, year of publication, and characteristics of the target population of the clinical studies that have used validated PRO-DEQs.

Design

Scoping review of the literature.

Methods

Searches were conducted in PubMed to retrieve PRO-DEQs published up to July 2018 and written in English, French, Italian or Spanish.

Results

One thousand six hundred two records were identified and 973 were included in the final analysis. Of these, 56 provided information on the design and validation of PRO-DEQs and 49 PRO-DEQs were identified. Twenty-two PRO-DEQs were validated (17 original and 5 modified) and 27 had no associated design, validity, and reliability studies. Most of the validated PRO-DEQs were designed in English, the number of items varies from 1 to 57, the dimensions are generally not specified, and they are self-administered. The greatest use of validated PRO-DEQs in clinical studies has been in Asia since 2010, with the Ocular Surface Disease Index being the most used. These questionnaires have been used mostly in adults, retired professionals, and people with visual diseases to diagnose DED.

Conclusions

This study aims to encourage the use of validated PRO-DEQs to guarantee the quality of the results obtained and the comparability and replicability among studies.

records.title: In vitro study examining the effectiveness of antiseptic prophylaxis for antibiotic-resistant bacterial endophthalmitis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: In vitro study examining the effectiveness of antiseptic prophylaxis for antibiotic-resistant bacterial endophthalmitis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To assess the effectiveness of current antiseptic agents on multidrug-resistant (MDR) isolates in an in vitro setting.

Setting

Department of Microbiology, The National Maternity Hospital, Dublin, Ireland.

Design

Organisms were selected based on current review of endophthalmitis literature: methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE), Pseudomonas aeruginosa, carbapenem-resistant and extended-spectrum β-lactamase Klebsiella pneumoniae, and vancomycin-resistant (VRE) Enterococcus faecalis.

Methods

Samples were exposed to povidone-iodine (PVI) 5% and chlorhexidine (CHX) 0.05% for 0.5 minutes, 1 minute, 3 minutes, and 5 minutes. After inactivation, organisms were incubated under standard conditions and growth assessed after 16 hours.

Results

MRSA and MRSE responded to 3-minute PVI exposure. CHX eradicated MRSA growth after 5 minutes but failed to completely suppress MRSE. Pseudomonas and Klebsiella required 3-minute CHX exposure and 5-minute PVI exposure for complete clearance. Eradication of enterococci (VRE positive and negative) was not achieved at 10 minutes of CHX or PVI exposure. Comparison of PVI vs CHX showed a benefit for PVI in MRSA (P < .01) and MRSE (P < .001) eradication at 3 minutes.

Conclusions

Current recommendations of 3 minutes of antisepsis prior to intraocular surgery are not sufficient for complete eradication of MDR organisms from the ocular surface. A bespoke approach is suggested to patients at risk for carriage of MDR organisms to minimize the risk of endophthalmitis.

records.title: The Pattern of Retinal Ganglion Cell Loss in Wolfram Syndrome is Distinct From Mitochondrial Optic Neuropathies.

content.title: The Pattern of Retinal Ganglion Cell Loss in Wolfram Syndrome is Distinct From Mitochondrial Optic Neuropathies.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To describe the clinical phenotype of a cohort of patients with Wolfram syndrome (WS), focusing on the pattern of optic atrophy correlated with brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) measurements, as compared with patients with OPA1-related dominant optic atrophy (DOA).

Design

Retrospective, comparative cohort study.

Methods

We reviewed 25 patients with WS and 33 age-matched patients affected by OPA1-related DOA. Ophthalmologic, neurologic, endocrinologic, and MRI data from patients with WS were retrospectively retrieved. Ophthalmologic data were compared with data from patients with OPA1-related DOA and further analyzed for age dependency dividing patients in age quartiles. In a subgroup of patients with WS, we correlated the structural damage assessed by optical coherence tomography (OCT) with brain MRI morphologic measurements. Visual acuity (VA), visual field mean defect (MD), retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), and ganglion cell layer (GCL) thickness were assessed by OCT and MRI morphologic measurements of anterior and posterior visual pathways.

Results

Optic atrophy was present in 100% of patients with WS. VA, MD, and RNFL thickness loss were worse in patients with WS with a faster decline since early age as compared with patients with DOA, who displayed a more stable visual function over the years. Conversely, GCL sectors were overall thinner in patients with DOA since early age compared to patients with WS, in which GCL thickness started to decline later in life. The neuroradiologic subanalysis on 11 patients with WS exhibited bilateral thinning of the anterior optic pathway, especially the prechiasmatic optic nerves and optic tracts. Optic tract thinning was significantly correlated with GCL thickness but not with RNFL parameters.

Conclusions

Our results showed a generally more severe and diffuse degeneration of both anterior and posterior visual pathways in patients with WS, with fast deterioration of visual function and structural OCT parameters since early age. The pattern observed with OCT suggests that retinal ganglion cell axonal degeneration (ie, RNFL) precedes cellular body atrophy (ie, GCL) by about a decade. This differs substantially from DOA, in which a more stable visual function is evident with predominant early loss of GCL, indirectly supporting the lack of a primary mitochondrial dysfunction in patients with WS.

records.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.

content.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation.

Methods

The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report.

Results

On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology-in the form of Machine Learning (ML) models and other models specialized in image recognition and processing, such as Convolutional Neural Networks Visual Transformers (CNN-ViTs)-is increasingly being used in ophthalmology. This review summarizes the main AI applications for laser-assisted refractive surgery. Methods: A wide-ranging literature search on the PubMed and ISI Thompson Web of Science databases was conducted. Results: AI is an all-encompassing technological concept that refers to either specific applications of ML/CNN models, such as in keratoconus screening or diagnosis, or agentic/multimodal AI applications that process different data types using a variety of AI models. The most clinically established applications found were corneal ectasia and keratoconus screening, in which AI models can reliably exceed 95% diagnostic accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity; nomogram-derived laser ablation programming; optimization of ray-tracing calculations for ray-traced ablation profiles; patient screening and selection for refractive surgery; visual and refractive result prediction; assessment of postoperative corneal ectasia risk; detection of intraoperative complications; research on the laser coupling effect; and other applications such as monitoring eye rubbing behavior in corneal ectasia suspects. Thus, singular, specific applications of AI models have made the largest clinical contributions. These results must be interpreted with a comparison of internal versus external validation, calibration, and generalizability. Overall the technology is highly promising. Agentic/multimodal AI frameworks are currently being discussed, with pilot studies published and applicability proposed in the context of large, high-patient-volume clinical practices. The technological advent of SHAP force plot graphs and saliency maps has improved understanding of the factors that contribute mechanistically to AI model reasoning, leading to more informed clinical decisions or research applicability, such as in finding parameters or factors linked to postoperative ectasia. Conclusions: AI is already established in laser-assisted refractive surgery in the form of models specialized in data-intensive analysis. At present, the best-performing novel AI models originate from the domain of large or multi-hospital settings due to requirements for multiple latest-generation diagnostic devices, high-volume patient data, computing expertise, and resources. Future directions could include clinical standardization and trickle-down dissemination of the technology. Agentic/multimodal AI has the potential to benefit large clinical/patient settings or offer access to expert knowledge in smaller practice settings. Agentic/multimodal AI implementation is offset by challenges in complexity, the technological limitations of LLMs ("hallucinations"), and ethical and legislative factors.

records.title: Deep Learning Model for Image-Based Classification of Four Keratitis Categories.

content.title: Deep Learning Model for Image-Based Classification of Four Keratitis Categories.
content.abstract:
Purpose

CorneAI was developed to classify anterior segment conditions into 9 categories. We aimed to develop a deep learning (DL) model for image-based classification among 4 selected keratitis categories: catarrhal ulcer, herpes stromal keratitis, peripheral ulcerative keratitis (PUK), and phlyctenular keratitis.

Methods

We retrospectively collected 973 anterior segment images from 576 patients at 7 institutions in Japan and the Japan Ocular Imaging Registry. A YOLOv5 model was developed and evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. In an exploratory analysis, 17 ophthalmologists classified 192 images from 1 randomly selected validation fold.

Results

The positive predictive values (95% confidence interval) were 0.72 (0.59-0.83) for catarrhal ulcer, 0.84 (0.77-0.89) for herpes stromal keratitis, 0.88 (0.85-0.91) for PUK, and 0.72 (0.65-0.77) for phlyctenular keratitis. The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.81 (0.74-0.87), 0.90 (0.87-0.93), 0.94 (0.93-0.96), and 0.91 (0.88-0.93), respectively. Sensitivity and specificity were 0.47 (0.37-0.58) and 0.98 (0.97-0.99) for catarrhal ulcer, 0.72 (0.65-0.79) and 0.97 (0.95-0.98) for herpes stromal keratitis, 0.93 (0.91-0.95) and 0.87 (0.84-0.90) for PUK, and 0.81 (0.75-0.86) and 0.91 (0.89-0.93) for phlyctenular keratitis. In an exploratory analysis, the diagnostic accuracies were 76.6% (95% CI, 70.1%-82.0%) for YOLOv5, 72.5 ± 9.3% (range, 53.6%-80.2%; n = 7) for corneal specialists, and 64.5 ± 10.2% (range, 45.3%-78.1%; n = 10) for ophthalmology residents.

Conclusions

We developed a DL model for image-based classification among 4 selected keratitis categories. Further validation in broader clinical populations, including other corneal diseases and normal corneas, is required before clinical application.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in odontology education.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in odontology education.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored in dental education as a tool to support teaching, learning, assessment, and clinical decision-making. This systematic review synthesized current evidence on the implementation and educational impact of AI technologies in undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing dental education.

Methodology

A PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted using Scopus, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore. Studies published between 2020 and 2025 evaluating AI applications in dental education were identified using predefined PICO criteria. Educational outcomes included knowledge acquisition, diagnostic accuracy, clinical reasoning, procedural skills, learner engagement, and perceptions of AI-assisted learning.

Results

The included literature reflects an expansion from machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision systems primarily evaluated for diagnostic support toward generative AI platforms, including large language models and retrieval-augmented generation systems. Across the included studies, AI applications were frequently associated with favorable diagnostic and examination performance and, in selected educational contexts, with supportive findings related to clinical reasoning, technical competency, feedback, and self-directed learning. However, the evidence was predominantly based on technical performance assessments and observational or cross-sectional designs.

Discussion

AI is increasingly being explored as a potential complementary educational resource, with applications including interactive tutoring, adaptive learning, and support for clinical reasoning. Nevertheless, heterogeneous methodologies and limited longitudinal evidence indicate the need for standardized educational evaluation and responsible curricular integration.

Conclusion

AI shows potential as a complementary resource in dental education. Its integration should remain pedagogically guided and ethically supervised while future research establishes its educational effectiveness through standardized and longitudinal evaluation.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: One step beyond CASA Systems: Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning (DL) for canine sperm analysis (CSA).

content.title: One step beyond CASA Systems: Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning (DL) for canine sperm analysis (CSA).
content.abstract: Computer Assisted Sperm Analysis (CASA) systems have become indispensable tools for determinining objective motility (percentage) and precise kinematic parameters (velocities μm/sec) in mammalian semen analysis over the past decades. However, conventional CASA platforms dependent on grayscale image acquisition and predefined mathematical algorithms. These rigid frameworks are often inadequate for capturing the complex, dynamic movement patterns of spermatozoa. In canine reproduction, where semen quality asssessment critical for Breeding Soundness Examinations (BSEs), Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART), and clinical decision making, these limitations may compromise the accuracy and clinical relevance of motility based diagnostics. Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Deep Learning (DL) offer transformative opportunities to overcome the intrinsic constraints of conventional CASA systems. AI/DL based approaches enable data driven feature extraction, improved sperm detection and superior tracking capabilities. Unlike traditional CASAs, AI/DL integrated systems, having been recently developed provide robust classification of motility patterns without strict dependence on manually defined thresholds, reducing sensitivity to variables such as illumination, magnification and background extender and seminal plasma (SP) or spermatogenesis based particiles. Moreover, DL models can simultaneously integrate spatial, temporal and morphological information as specialized datasets expand. This article summarized the current state of the art in conventional (gray scale) and modern (AI/DL) canine CASA applications and critically discusses their methodological limitations based on studies published between 2013 and 2026, also covering researches and development pathway related with three successive projects: ESAS (2014-2018)_conventional/ESAS TİP (2018-2022)_AI-DL and ESAS TÜG_AI-DL (initiated 2022 and in progress) partly financially and scientifically supported by The Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (TÜBİTAK) and Technology and Innovation Funding Programmes Directorate (TEYDEB) (2013-2018 conventional, 2018-2026 AI/DL model R&D studies, especially 1507 and TÜBİTAK TEYDEB 1501 R&D Program (ESAS Commercial Product Development (TÜG) Project No: 3230063)). This current article highlights the technological transition from fragmented, parameter based motility assessments toward holistic, pattern oriented sperm evaluations, evaluating its ultimate implications for fertility prediction and routine canine veterinary andrology with one step beyond of conventional CASA with deep learning and artificial intelligence.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in glaucoma diagnosis and management: a systematic review of the past decade (2015-2026).

content.title: Artificial intelligence in glaucoma diagnosis and management: a systematic review of the past decade (2015-2026).
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to support glaucoma detection and monitoring, with rapid advances in deep learning, multimodal imaging, and longitudinal prediction. This review evaluates the evidence supporting these developments and identifies barriers to clinical translation.

Areas covered

A systematic search of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink was conducted following PRISMA guidelines, with the protocol registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261450819). Of 3,758 records identified, 63 eligible peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2026 were included. The review examined AI techniques, imaging modalities, datasets, diagnostic and predictive performance, validation strategies, and reported limitations in Glaucoma care. Most studies used deep learning applied to fundus photography, optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography, visual fields, or multimodal data. Many models achieved an area under the ROC curve of approximately 0.95.

Expert opinion

AI has substantial potential to improve glaucoma detection and monitoring, but high reported accuracy alone does not establish clinical readiness. Prospective multicenter validation using diverse populations, explainable and reproducible models, standardized evaluation, and integration into clinical workflows are essential before widespread implementation.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.

content.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been significantly improved through deep learning techniques; however, the lack of interpretability remains a major challenge for clinical adoption. Methods: This study proposes an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-driven framework for multiclass brain tumor classification using a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) and four transfer learning models, namely ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0. The models were trained and evaluated on a publicly available brain MRI dataset consisting of glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor classes. Their classification performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and confusion matrix analysis. To enhance transparency and interpretability, Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP were used to visualize and quantify the regions contributing to the classification decisions. Results: Experimental results state that the transfer learning models consistently outperformed the CNN by learning more discriminative feature representations while producing more localized and interpretable explanations. The agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirms that the proposed models predominantly relied on tumor regions rather than irrelevant background information, thereby improving the interpretability and reliability of the diagnostic predictions. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides an effective and explainable computer-aided diagnosis system that supports trustworthy deep learning-based brain tumor classification and has the potential for decision-making.

records.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of a large language model in assessing spirometry test acceptability and interpretation: a performance study.

content.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of a large language model in assessing spirometry test acceptability and interpretation: a performance study.
content.abstract:
Background

Spirometry is one of the most used pulmonary function tests for assessing respiratory function and diagnosing ventilatory disorders in clinical practice. Evaluation of test validity and interpretation is typically performed by trained healthcare professionals. The present study aims to evaluate the capability of a publicly available large language model (LLM) to perform quality assurance and interpretations of spirometry tests.

Methods

A total of 150 spirometry tests were retrospectively collected from the pulmonary function laboratories. The spirometry tests were evaluated for acceptability and interpreted by clinicians according to ATS/ERS recommendations as part of standard clinical practice. Subsequently, a publicly available LLM (ChatGPT 5.5) was prompted to evaluate the acceptability and interpret the same spirometry tests according to ATS/ERS criteria. The model interpreted each spirometry test on three separate occasions for assessing reproducibility. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were calculated by comparing LLM assessments with clinician assessments of spirometry test acceptability and interpretation.

Results

For spirometry acceptability evaluation, ChatGPT demonstrated an overall accuracy of 87% (95% CI: 81%-92%), sensitivity of 91% (95% CI: 85%-95%), specificity of 61% (95% CI 39%-80%), PPV of 94% (95% CI: 89%-97%), and NPV of 48(95% CI: 29%-67%) with Cohen's k of 0.46. The spiromteric interpretation agreement with the clinicians reference standard was moderate, with exact agreement of 0.61 (95% CI: 0.54-0.69) while Cohen's Kappa (Unweighted) was 0.47 (95% CI: 0.37-0.56) and Macro F1 score was 0.39 (95% CI: 0.33-0.49). Reproducibility across three independent trials was moderate (Fleiss' κ 0.58). Class-specific interpretation performance varied by category; sensitivity was highest for normal pattern and restrictive defects (0.72), whereas sensitivity for obstructive defects was 0.27. F1-scores were highest for normal and restrictive defects (0.81 and 0.62, respectively).

Conclusion

The current findings suggest that ChatGPT 5.5 has a limited capability, at its current stage of development, to serve as a reliable tool for independent spirometry interpretation in clinical practice. Nevertheless, it may serve as an adjunct to clinical decision-making and educational tools. Prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.

content.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in dermatophytosis: Toward better clinical diagnosis and management.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in dermatophytosis: Toward better clinical diagnosis and management.
content.abstract: Dermatophytosis is one of the most common superficial fungal infections worldwide. However, its diagnosis and management remain challenging because its clinical manifestations often overlap with those of other dermatoses, conventional mycological tests have inherent limitations, the disease is prone to recurrence, and antifungal resistance has received increasing attention. This review summarizes current applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in dermatophytosis, with a focus on the use of machine learning and deep learning in clinical photographs, non-invasive skin imaging, and laboratory diagnostics, while also discussing their roles in treatment support, follow-up assessment, patient education, and adherence management. In addition, with the accumulation of molecular diagnostic, mass spectrometric, and epidemiological data, AI may also provide auxiliary support for extended applications such as resistance risk recognition. Current evidence suggests that AI can improve the efficiency, consistency, and objectivity of dermatophytosis diagnosis and provide quantitative support for treatment response assessment and long-term follow-up. With further improvement in research quality and the accumulation of clinical application experience, AI is expected to become increasingly integrated into dermatophytosis management workflows.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in the in vitro fertilization laboratory: A scoping review and SWOT-based evaluation of emerging applications.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in the in vitro fertilization laboratory: A scoping review and SWOT-based evaluation of emerging applications.
content.abstract:
Objective

Artificial intelligence (AI) represents a potentially transformative tool in assisted reproductive technology (ART), particularly in vitro fertilization (IVF), for gamete assessment, embryo selection, non-invasive genetic testing, and laboratory automation. This scoping review synthesized recent evidence on AI applications in IVF laboratories and evaluated their translational maturity using an evidence maturity framework and a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis.

Methods

This scoping review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed studies published from January 2020 to February 2025. Eligible studies evaluated AI, machine learning, or deep learning in laboratory components of ART. Data were charted on AI methods, dataset characteristics, validation strategies, clinical endpoints, and performance metrics.

Results

Ninety-four studies were included. Most applications addressed embryo grading and implantation prediction using convolutional neural networks and were evaluated through internal cross-validation. Reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranged from 0.75 to 0.92, depending on the endpoint and dataset size. AI applications in sperm analysis and oocyte assessment showed greater reproducibility than manual evaluation. Non-invasive genetic prediction models displayed promising but heterogeneous sensitivity and remained predominantly limited to internal validation. Few studies reported prospective evaluation or external validation using multicenter datasets.

Conclusion

AI applications in IVF are expanding, but most remain at early stages of clinical translation. Standardized datasets, external validation, interpretable algorithms, and regulatory oversight remain necessary for safe, equitable clinical integration. AI should function as a decision-support tool that supplements, rather than replaces, embryologists' expertise.

records.title: A review of deep learning applications on histopathologic and genomic data in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.

content.title: A review of deep learning applications on histopathologic and genomic data in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
content.abstract: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis explains the histological pattern of injury seen through light microscopy in kidney biopsy specimens and is the end result of different injuries to podocytes. The clinical classification of patients by FSGS lesion is challenging because of a broad spectrum of etiologies, limited understanding of pathophysiology, and poor correlation among histopathology, treatment response, and clinical outcomes. Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis is a problematic process to detect lesions, with low and late analysis of the absence of initial symptoms, and a challenging position of specific markers. However, Histopathological and genomic Data in Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) are significantly used in multiple research applications, but they face several limitations that restrict the efficiency of experimental analysis. This review systematically analyzed recent enhancements in biopsy-based analysis and deep learning models for FSGS, with specific emphasis on different mechanisms. Moreover, this review analyzed different strategies, namely kidney transplantation, pathogenesis to therapeutic approaches, transformer-based architectures, glomerular segmentation methodologies, multitasking strategy classification, and gene expression analysis for FSGS. This review analysis includes 121 research papers, which are selected and analyzed for glomerular segmentation, gene expression, clinical outcomes, lesion classification, and disease recurrence prediction. Based on the recent research frameworks, it explicitly states the performance analysis, benefits, as well as challenges of FSGS. The article presents details of a new dataset and future directions for improving the majority of nephropathology diagnoses previously available through the use of integrated approaches that utilize both histopathology and genomics, enhancing future research direction in FSGS.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Methods in Stroke Prediction: A Narrative Review.
records.publisher: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology

content.title: Artificial Intelligence Methods in Stroke Prediction: A Narrative Review.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Despite rising healthcare costs, early noninvasive stroke risk stratification via artificial intelligence provides accurate, rapid predictions, establishing AI as a powerful tool in healthcare by enabling tailored treatment for stroke patients. Traditional algorithms assess risk using regression-based statistical correlations, which, while practical and user-friendly, show moderate predictive accuracy. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models effectively identify individuals at higher risk of stroke across diverse populations, enabling timely intervention. However, evidence summarizing the effectiveness of these approaches remains sparse. This review presents various ML and DL algorithms, clarifying their theoretical foundations, historical evolution, and applications in stroke prediction. This narrative review focuses on studies published within the last five years and emphasizes the clinical relevance and translational potential of AI-based stroke prediction models.

records.title: AI in orthodontic treatment planning: a systematic review comparing learning approaches.

content.title: AI in orthodontic treatment planning: a systematic review comparing learning approaches.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence has increasingly been applied to orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning. Clinical decision-making in orthodontics is complex and often varies among practitioners, particularly for decisions such as tooth extraction, skeletal classification, and selection of treatment modality. This systematic review aimed to evaluate how artificial intelligence and knowledge-based systems have been developed and assessed for orthodontic treatment planning, to compare their performance with expert clinicians, and to examine how different learning approaches influence accuracy, interpretability, and potential clinical integration.

Methods

A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and IEEE Xplore was conducted from database inception to 15 October 2025 without language or date restrictions. Eligible studies evaluated artificial intelligence-based or knowledge-based systems using real orthodontic patient data to support diagnosis or treatment planning. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the ROBINS-I tool. Due to heterogeneity in study designs, decision tasks, and outcome measures, findings were synthesized narratively rather than through meta-analysis.

Results

Nineteen studies met inclusion criteria. Most investigated supervised machine-learning models for extraction decisions, skeletal classification, or multi-step treatment planning, while others evaluated rule-based, fuzzy, Bayesian, or hybrid systems. Reported accuracies frequently exceeded 80%, and in some studies surpassed 90% when compared with expert decisions. Knowledge-based systems, including rule-based, fuzzy, and Bayesian/probabilistic approaches, offered greater transparency in reasoning, whereas data-driven models often demonstrated higher discriminative performance. Overall risk of bias was predominantly moderate to serious, largely due to retrospective designs, single-center samples, limited external validation, and reliance on expert opinion as the reference standard.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence systems can approximate expert orthodontic decision-making for defined diagnostic and planning tasks and show promise as clinical decision-support tools. However, current evidence is limited by methodological weaknesses and lack of prospective validation. These systems should presently be considered adjunctive aids rather than autonomous planners. Robust multicenter studies with external validation are needed before routine clinical implementation can be recommended.

Trial registration

PROSPERO 1025581. Registered prospectively.

records.title: Lung cancer diagnosis from CT scans using artificial intelligence techniques: A global perspective.

content.title: Lung cancer diagnosis from CT scans using artificial intelligence techniques: A global perspective.
content.abstract:
Objective

In this research, we conducted a systematic review of artificial intelligence techniques used for the diagnosis of lung cancer.

Methods

A systematic search of Web of Science, PubMed, Scopus, Epistemonikos, Cochrane, Medline, and Embase databases was carried out, containing the literature published up to June 2025. Prediction model risk of bias assessment tool (PROBAST) was used to evaluate the risk of bias and applicability of the diagnostic model studies included in the current research.

Results

204 studies were included. The included articles utilized various AI techniques, including CNN (Convolutional Neural Network), SVM (Support Vector Machine), RF (Random Forest), KNN (K-Nearest Neighbor), PM-DL (Pattern Matching combined with Deep Learning), ANN (Artificial Neural Network), DNN (Deep Neural Network), CDNs (Convolutional Dense Networks), DLS (Deep Learning System), LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory), NNE (Neural Network Ensemble), and LDA (Linear Discriminant Analysis). The CNN model appears to be the most commonly used model in the papers. It was observed that applying deep learning models to preprocessed and augmented medical images led to improved performance metrics, including AUC, sensitivity, and accuracy. The accuracy of artificial intelligence techniques ranged from 68.4 to 100, while the sensitivity varied from 50.0 to 100. The specificity of the artificial intelligence techniques ranged from 50.0 to 100. The AUC of the artificial intelligence techniques ranged from 61.0 % to 100 %, while the recall varied from 75.0 to 99.82.

Conclusion

This research accentuates the potential of artificial intelligence techniques in the diagnosis and detection of lung cancer, with diverse levels of diagnostic accuracy. Additional research is required to optimize these artificial intelligence techniques, as well as to ascertain their clinical relevance and appropriateness in real-world clinical applicability.

records.title: Effects of exercise intensity and volume on systemic inflammation in overweight and obese postmenopausal women: a dose-response meta-analysis.

content.title: Effects of exercise intensity and volume on systemic inflammation in overweight and obese postmenopausal women: a dose-response meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

This study evaluates the dose-response relationships between multiple exercise parameters (volume, duration, and intensity) and inflammatory modulation (C-reactive protein [CRP], interleukin-6 [IL-6], tumor necrosis factor-α [TNF-α], and adiponectin) exclusively in overweight and obese postmenopausal women.

Methods

Five databases were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) up to January 2026 (PROSPERO: CRD420261288134). Standardized Mean Differences (SMD) were estimated using random-effects models. Meta-regression analyses investigated the dose-response effects of total exercise volume (MET-minutes/week), intervention duration (weeks), and exercise intensity (systematically standardized to %HRmax).

Results

Analysis of 30 RCTs (N = 2,124) demonstrated that exercise interventions significantly reduced TNF-α (SMD = -0.47, p < 0.001) and CRP (SMD = -0.36, p = 0.001). Changes in IL-6 and adiponectin were not statistically significant. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses confirmed the exceptional stability of the CRP (SMD range: -0.41 to -0.28) and TNF-α reductions. Meta-regression revealed no definitive linear dose-response relationships for total exercise volume or duration across any biomarkers. However, a borderline trend (p = 0.063) indicated that higher exercise intensity is associated with greater reductions in TNF-α.

Conclusion

Structured exercise functions as a potent therapeutic modality that reliably mitigates systemic and tissue-derived inflammation in postmenopausal obesity. The findings challenge the traditional reliance on total exercise volume or duration, pointing instead toward an "intensity threshold" where higher exercise intensities more effectively drive anti-inflammatory adaptations. Precision exercise prescriptions for this demographic should prioritize the optimization of exercise intensity.

records.title: Imaging studies for predicting hematoma expansion: from traditional imaging signs to artificial intelligence-based multimodal fusion.

content.title: Imaging studies for predicting hematoma expansion: from traditional imaging signs to artificial intelligence-based multimodal fusion.
content.abstract: Hematoma expansion (HE) is a critical and modifiable event following acute intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Predicting HE accurately can inform individualized treatment and improve patient outcomes. This review systematically outlines the evolution of imaging-based HE prediction. We first define the core concepts of traditional HE, revised HE (rHE), and ultra-early hematoma growth (uHG). We then summarize predictive studies that employ traditional imaging markers, such as the computed tomography angiography (CTA) spot sign, non-contrast CT (NCCT) signs, and combined clinical-imaging scoring systems. Subsequent sections focus on AI-driven methodologies, encompassing radiomics, deep learning, and multi-task learning. The discussion extends to precision prediction through multimodal data fusion and subgroup analyses based on hemorrhage location and onset time. Finally, we address persistent challenges, including model interpretability, generalizability, and translational gaps, and suggest future directions involving federated learning, explainable AI, dynamic prediction, and closed-loop decision systems. This review offers a structured framework to guide both clinical practice and future research.

records.title: Cataract and glaucoma surgery in microphthalmic, nanophthalmic, and high hyperopic eyes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Cataract and glaucoma surgery in microphthalmic, nanophthalmic, and high hyperopic eyes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates refractive error (RE), visual acuity (VA), intraocular pressure (IOP), and anterior chamber depth (ACD) outcomes following surgical procedures in adults (≥ 18 years) with nanophthalmos, microphthalmos, and high hyperopia.

Clinical relevance

Nanophthalmos, microphthalmos, and high hyperopia are a spectrum of anatomic variants characterized by short axial length and crowded anterior segment. These features create significant risks for angle-closure glaucoma and complex cataract surgery. As existing literature is fragmented and limited to small case series, this study provides a comprehensive evaluation of surgical safety and efficacy in these high-risk populations.

Methods

Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, a search was conducted across five databases (Cochrane, PubMed, Scopus, Ovid MEDLINE, and Embase via Ovid) for studies published between January 2010 and December 2024. Eligible studies reported original clinical data on surgical interventions for adult (≥ 18 years) patients with nanophthalmos, microphthalmos, or high hyperopia with concomitant cataract or glaucoma. Meta-analysis, subgroup analysis, and meta-regression were performed to assess changes in RE, VA, IOP, and ACD.

Results

Meta-analysis of 21 articles involving 957 patients (1,110 eyes) suggests that surgical intervention is associated with improvement in clinical parameters across a spectrum of short eyes. Standalone phacoemulsification significantly reduced RE in nanophthalmic eyes (mean difference (MD) = -13.20 diopters (D); 95% confidence interval (CI): -15.19, -11.22; Q = 3.51, p = 0.48, I2 = 0.0%) at medium-term follow-up and in high hyperopic eyes (MD = -9.23 D; 95% CI: -15.02, -3.45; Q = 322.19, p < 0.001, I2 = 97.8%) at medium-term follow-up with high heterogeneity in the effects. Standalone phacoemulsification significantly improved VA in nanophthalmic eyes at both short-term (MD = -0.66 logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution (logMAR); 95% CI: -1.30, -0.02; Q = 98.45, p < 0.001, I2 = 97.0%) and medium-term (MD = -0.70 logMAR; 95% CI: -1.30, -0.09; Q = 97.14, p < 0.001, I2 = 93.8%) follow-up with high heterogeneity in the effects. In contrast, phacoemulsification + filtering surgery resulted in a significant worsening in VA at short-term follow-up for nanophthalmic eyes (MD = 0.28 logMAR; 95% CI: 0.21, 0.35; Q = 1.24, p = 0.27, I2 = 19.4%). Significant IOP reduction was achieved primarily through combined procedures in both nanophthalmic and microphthalmic eyes. Presence of concomitant glaucoma was associated with a greater reduction in IOP across all axial lengths. Significant ACD deepening was achieved across all axial lengths (MD = 1.30 millimeters (mm), 95% CI: 0.86, 1.74; Q = 244.55, p < 0.001, I2 = 99.3%) with high heterogeneity in the effects. Meta-regression identified a significant study-level association between mean age and post-operative RE (multiple adjusted coefficient: 10.72, p = 0.001). No effect of race was detectable in this study-level meta-regression, although power was limited.

Conclusion

Surgical interventions in adults with nanophthalmos, microphthalmos, and high hyperopia were associated with meaningful improvements in RE, VA, IOP, and ACD, although outcomes varied by underlying diagnosis and procedure type. Standalone phacoemulsification consistently improved refractive and anatomical outcomes, particularly in nanophthalmos and high hyperopia, while combined procedures incorporating vitrectomy or filtering surgery achieved greater IOP reduction in eyes with concomitant glaucoma. Subgroup analyses suggested that shorter axial length and the presence of glaucoma influenced treatment response. However, substantial heterogeneity across studies and frequent post-operative complications highlight the need for standardized surgical protocols and higher-quality prospective studies to better define optimal management strategies for these anatomically complex eyes.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251033701, identifier CRD420251033701.

records.title: Transcatheter arterial chemoembolization combined with stereotactic body radiation therapy versus transcatheter arterial chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Transcatheter arterial chemoembolization combined with stereotactic body radiation therapy versus transcatheter arterial chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

The optimal integration of locoregional therapies for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains an area of active investigation. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of combining transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) with stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) compared to TACE.

Methods

A comprehensive literature search was conducted across five databases up to March 1, 2026. Eligible studies compared TACE combined with SBRT versus TACE (with or without concurrent systemic therapy) for unresectable HCC. The primary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS), with treatment-related adverse events (CTCAE grade ≥3) as a key safety outcome. Pooled hazard ratios (HR) and risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q test and the I² statistic. Subgroup analyses (by study design, concurrent systemic therapy, and HR adjustment) and sensitivity analyses were performed.

Results

Nine studies involving 828 patients were included. The TACE-SBRT combination significantly improved OS (HR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.35-0.65, P < 0.001; I² = 13%) and PFS (HR = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.32-0.65, P < 0.001; I² = 54%) compared to TACE. There was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of grade ≥3 adverse events between the two groups (RR = 1.27, 95% CI: 0.87-1.86, P = 0.21). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings.

Conclusion

In patients with unresectable HCC, the combination of TACE and SBRT appears to confer a survival advantage over TACE, without significantly increasing the risk of severe adverse events.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261350374, identifier CRD 420261350374.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in predicting anesthetic complications: current techniques, clinical applications, and limitations.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in predicting anesthetic complications: current techniques, clinical applications, and limitations.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing anesthesiology by enhancing the prediction and management of perioperative complications, including intraoperative hypotension, respiratory failure, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), and pain control challenges. This scoping review synthesizes evidence from 82 studies, identified through a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and grey literature from January 2010 to September 2025, to map AI techniques, their clinical applications, and limitations. Techniques include Machine Learning (ML) (e.g., random forests, support vector machines), deep learning, natural language processing (NLP), Computer Vision, Bayesian models, and fuzzy logic, applied across preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative phases. AI models achieve superior predictive accuracy (AUC 0.85-0.94) compared to traditional methods (AUC 0.76-0.88), enabling early detection of complications and reducing opioid use by 15-35%. Applications include preoperative risk stratification, intraoperative monitoring, and postoperative analgesia optimization. Challenges include algorithmic bias, data reliability, interoperability, and real-time integration barriers. Ethical considerations emphasize transparency, equity, and clinician oversight. This review positions AI as a decision-support tool within the P4 medicine framework (Predictive, Preventive, Personalized, Participatory), advocating for validation, ethical frameworks, and integration with anesthesia information management systems (AIMS) to enhance perioperative safety.

records.title: The anxiolytic effect of dexmedetomidine in adult perioperative patients: a systematic review with meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

content.title: The anxiolytic effect of dexmedetomidine in adult perioperative patients: a systematic review with meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
content.abstract:
Background

Perioperative anxiety in adults is common and impairs postoperative recovery. The use of dexmedetomidine during perioperative procedures is increasing, but evidence on its effects on anxiety-related outcomes remains to be systematically synthesized.

Methods

This systematic review was based on searches of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library from database inception through May 4, 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials evaluating perioperative dexmedetomidine in adults and reporting quantitative anxiety outcomes.

Results

Twelve RCTs involving 1,373 participants were included. Overall anxiety scores were lower with dexmedetomidine than with control (SMD = -0.73; 95% CI [-1.37, -0.10]; P = 0.028; I² = 94.2%; 95% prediction interval [-2.97, 1.50]). Within 24 h after surgery, the pooled estimate likewise favored dexmedetomidine (6 RCTs; SMD = -0.83; 95% CI [-1.58, -0.07]; P = 0.038; I² = 92.9%; 95% prediction interval [-2.76, 1.11]). The estimates for intraoperative anxiety, anxiety at 24-72 h postoperatively, and anxiety beyond 72 h were SMDs = 0.08 (95% CI [-2.31, 2.46]), -0.11 (95% CI [-0.41, 0.20]), and -0.31 (95% CI [-1.02, 0.39]), respectively. Postoperative sleep quality favored dexmedetomidine (4 RCTs; SMD = -0.64; 95% CI [-0.81, -0.48]; I² = 0%), whereas no clear between-group differences were observed for depression or pain.

Conclusion

Perioperative dexmedetomidine was associated with reduced anxiety in adult surgical patients. Although the evidence for this association was clearer within 24 h after surgery, the limited data across time windows do not establish that the anxiolytic effect is confined to this period.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251129414.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cardiology: Applications in Diagnosis and Risk Prediction.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cardiology: Applications in Diagnosis and Risk Prediction.
content.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) continue to be a major cause of death and morbidity throughout the world, and there is an increasing need for better diagnostic and predictive approaches. Existing methods do not fully reflect complex clinical interactions, and new computational methods possess greater capabilities. The limitations, including a lack of diversity in datasets, low generalizability, and limited interpretability, limit general use in the clinic. The review highlights the latest developments in artificial intelligence (AI) for diagnosing and predicting cardiovascular risk factors, with a focus on its clinical applications and current challenges. A literature review was conducted on machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) applications in imaging, electrocardiography (ECG), and predictive modeling. AI has been shown to improve diagnostic accuracy, facilitate earlier diagnosis, and enhance the ability to stratify disease risk compared with traditional methods. The seamless integration with wearable technologies ensures continuous monitoring and proactive management. While these developments help to ensure more accurate and individualized care, there are issues of validation, ethics, and integration. Moreover, integration of multi-modal data sources and real-time analytics enhances clinical decision-making and risk assessment. As technology continues to evolve, its scalability and applicability across various healthcare settings are expected to improve. In summary, AI has the potential to revolutionize cardiovascular care and enhance clinical outcomes by leveraging data-driven approaches.

records.title: [Clinical applications and future perspectives of artificial intelligence-enabled surgical robots in gastrointestinal surgery].
records.publisher: Zhonghua wei chang wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of gastrointestinal surgery

content.title: [Clinical applications and future perspectives of artificial intelligence-enabled surgical robots in gastrointestinal surgery].
